jobs.description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Key job responsibilities
- Review, update, and approve equipment submittals
- Work with global liquid cooling equipment suppliers and manufacturers
- Build trust and relationships with different stakeholders (e.g. reliability, operations, design, compliance)
- Work on concurrent projects, in multiple geographic zones
- Understand and explain complex systems in clear and concise language
- Develop Product Roadmaps
- Listen to the voice of the customer to understand technical and business requirements
- Work with global supplier and manufacturers to design new products
- Contribute to our global body of knowledge and drive a cycle of continuous improvement at a global scale
- Ability and willingness to travel domestic and internationally for up to 25% of the year

A day in the life
Our Technical Product Managers work closely with key partners to innovate, create, manage, and deliver world class products to be deployed in our data centers. Our product manager work passionately to define customer requirements, development compelling product strategies to drive business value, and partner with cross functional teams and external vendors to make their strategies a reality at AWS scale!

About the team
Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture

jobs.title: Sr. Product Manager - Technical, QoS & Performance , Leo Network Infrastructure
jobs.description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable broadband connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From households to small businesses, schools, hospitals, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve communities and organizations operating in places without dependable internet access.

We are seeking a Senior Product Manager - Technical (PMT) to own the Quality of Service (QoS) and Performance domain within Leo Networking. In this role, you will define the products and features that ensure Leo delivers on its performance promises — from core performance assurance to traffic shaping and congestion management algorithms. You will work at the intersection of networking engineering, satellite systems, and customer experience to build differentiated, measurable, and enforceable Performance & QoS capabilities.

This is a high-visibility role that requires deep technical acumen in networking, strong product sense, and the ability to influence across engineering, business, and leadership. You will own the Performance and QoS roadmap from concept through launch, write PRFAQs and technical requirements, and represent the customer’s performance expectations in every architectural decision.

Key job responsibilities
Own the end-to-end Performance and QoS product strategy for Leo, including traffic classification, prioritization, shaping, and congestion management.

Define and drive the performance metrics framework — establishing SLAs, SLOs, and KPIs that govern throughput, latency, jitter, and packet loss across the Leo network.

Partner with Principal Engineers and SDEs to prioritize and implement network performance capabilities and enforcement mechanisms across the satellite, ground gateway, and SDN layers.

Write PRFAQs, technical narratives, and requirement documents to secure resources and align leadership on the network performance roadmap.

Collaborate with sales, demand management, and capacity management to gather customer performance requirements and translate them into product features.

Define acceptance criteria and performance gates for new feature performance capabilities, ensuring QoS compliance before customer-facing releases.

Work cross-functionally with the Beam Planning, SDN, and Satellite Operations teams to optimize resource allocation and minimize latency, packet loss, and congestion across the constellation.

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

A day in the life
Your morning starts with a review of overnight performance dashboards — checking throughput, latency percentiles, and congestion events across active beams and ground gateways. You notice a pattern in peak-hour congestion for a specific geographic region and draft a quick analysis to bring to your engineering sync.

Mid-morning, you’re in a design review with the SDN team, debating the trade-offs of a new traffic shaping algorithm that could improve P99 latency for enterprise customers but may impact other traffic. You push for a data-driven approach, proposing an A/B test framework to validate the change in a controlled environment.

After lunch, you’re on a call with an enterprise customer’s network architect who wants to understand how Amazon Leo’s quality of service compares to their existing MPLS-based WAN, and how to best integrate Leo connectivity in parallel to their existing MPLS WAN behind an SDWAN appliance. You walk them through Leo’s service plan tiers, SLA commitments, and the telemetry they’ll have access to.

In the afternoon, you’re drafting the PRFAQ for the next phase of network performance— introducing dynamic bandwidth allocation that adapts to real-time demand patterns. You collaborate with a principal engineer to ensure the technical approach is sound, and align with sales, capacity, and finance teams on the financial impact. You end the day with a quick sync with the Beam Planning team to review capacity forecasts for the upcoming month.

About the team
The Leo Connectivity Product team is responsible for the end-to-end networking stack that delivers connectivity from customer terminals through the satellite constellation to ground gateways and back to the terrestrial internet. We work across the control plane and data plane services that make Leo a carrier-grade networking provider.

Our team culture values deep technical curiosity, customer obsession, and a bias for action. We operate with a startup mentality inside Amazon — moving fast, iterating on data, and shipping capabilities that directly impact customer experience. We are builders who are energized by the challenge of delivering consistent, high-performance networking from a dynamic constellation of LEO satellites.

We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We believe the best products come from teams with varied perspectives and experiences.
Basic qualifications:
- Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition
- Experience contributing to engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product
- Experience in representing and advocating for a variety of critical customers and stakeholders during executive-level prioritization and planning
- Experience defining and managing SLAs/SLOs for networking or cloud services.
- Strong understanding of network performance fundamentals: IP DSCP, L2 CoS, traffic classification, marking, shaping, network queuing disciplines, fair queueing, CoDel, WRED, bufferbloat
- Track record of writing technical requirements documents, PRFAQs, or product specifications.
Preferred qualifications:

- Experience working across teams and influencing teams that are not your own
- Experience with satellite communications, LEO networking, or space-based systems.
- Experience in customer-facing technical product role at a cloud provider or telecommunications company.
- Familiarity with AWS networking services (Direct Connect, Transit Gateway, VPC) and how enterprise customers build hybrid networks.

jobs.description:
Amazon's Worldwide Global Selling team builds the products and programs that help sellers grow their businesses across Amazon's global marketplace network. Global from Day 1 (GfD) is among the most consequential bets in this space — a program designed to remove the friction, capital commitment, and compliance complexity that have historically made cross-border expansion out of reach for most sellers. Sellers list once. Amazon handles fulfillment, compliance, pricing, and returns across every market.

The Selection PM owns the growth engine that makes this work. We identify which products have cross-border demand potential, recruit them into the program, activate them to buyable status, and drive the selection quality that converts glances into sales. The decisions made here — on eligibility criteria, scoring signals, activation quality, and seller tooling — determine what GfD looks like at scale and how fast it gets there.

This is a high-ownership role with direct impact on one of Global Selling's most visible growth programs. The right candidate builds well under ambiguity, takes ownership of problems that don't yet have a clear solution, and is energized by a roadmap that is theirs to define.

Key job responsibilities
- Selection Recruitment: Define and drive the funnel that identifies eligible ASINs across the CN-origin FBA catalog, scores them for cross-border demand potential, and recruits sellers to enroll. Own the eligibility criteria, scoring signals, and targeting methodology — and the tooling that makes enrollment actionable at scale.

- Buyable ASIN Activation: Own the pipeline that turns enrolled ASINs into live, buyable, discoverable selection across GfD markets. Identify and systematically eliminate the blockers — compliance gaps, listing deficiencies, spec mismatches — that prevent ASINs from reaching buyable status.

- Selection Quality: Own the selection productivity funnel end to end — from enrolled ASIN to first sale. Define what good looks like, build the "Perfect ASIN" activation playbook, and drive the metrics that prove selection is converting, not just listed.

- Demand Intelligence & Scoring: Partner with science and data teams to build and refine the signals that predict cross-border demand potential. Translate model outputs into actionable seller-facing recommendations and enrollment prioritization.

- Seller-Facing Tooling: Collaborate with NGS and SX PMs to build the Seller Central surfaces that help sellers understand which products to expand globally, what's blocking their selection, and what to do next — making the right action obvious without requiring manual analysis.

A day in the life
our morning starts with the selection funnel — buyable rate, activation blockers, compliance stalls. You triage, escalate what needs it, and move on. Mid-morning you're with the science team pressure-testing a new demand scoring signal. After lunch, you're reviewing a seller-facing surface with the SX PM — pushing on information hierarchy, making sure the action lands before the explanation. Late afternoon is heads-down on the Perfect ASIN playbook: defining the activation standard the team will execute against at scale. No two days look the same. Most involve data, decisions, and moving something from blocked to shipped.

jobs.title: Sr Product Manager (Tech), SCOT-AIM
jobs.description:
Amazon’s SCOT-BizOps AI team is looking for an experienced Sr Product Manager (Tech) to conceptualize, articulate, and develop state of the art technology to measure and improve the shopping experience of every Amazon customer. The BizOps-AI team is a part of Amazon’s Supply Chain Optimization Technology (SCOT) organization, whose charter is to deliver the best possible customer experience and improve supply chain outcomes while maximizing the return on our inventory investment, fulfillment assets, and transportation network. We are never satisfied with the status quo and are convinced that there is always opportunity to innovate on behalf of customers.

Unlike brick and mortar stores where it is challenging to capture customer interest in a product unless they actually purchase the item, e-commerce offers the unique advantage of capturing customer "glance views" even if they don't convert to sales. Glance views, or GVs, are a leading indicator of potential future demand and allow us to capture a comprehensive set of data points (eg. price, delivery speed) to understand what we showed the customer and the resultant customer behavior. Amazon uses GV data to metricize and improve key performance indicators for customer experience like availability and promised delivery speed.

The person in this role will own Tier-1 CX and Supply chain metrics that provide stakeholders across Amazon with deep insights to identify and resolve defects. These metrics answer questions like: Was Amazon in stock on an item when customers were viewing it? Was the inventory in a location from where it could be immediately picked, packed, and shipped out to the customer? If not, what was the root cause? Your products will simplify the Business operations associated with these metrics, right from extracting insights from data, identifying opportunities for improvement, working with partner teams to deliver automated and scalable solutions, and providing regular performance/progress updates to stakeholders. You will build AI-powered solutions to automate repetitive tasks such as insight generation, identifying defects, debugging issues, developing/improving solutions for new use-cases and deploying fixes in production. This will involve managing the data infrastructure, software applications and CX interfaces.

The products you build will have a worldwide user base, spanning across multiple organizations that play a role in Amazon’s supply chain and the shopping experience we deliver to customer. You will own the process of first understanding what information is valuable to our internal customers and then working closely with our business intelligence, data engineering, and research science teams to deliver products that meet our customers’ needs in the long term. You will always be challenged to think several steps ahead so that the solutions you are building today will scale well with future growth and without adding excessive operational overhead. You will help define the product roadmap, serve as the voice of the customer, and champion your products across Amazon. You will work with worldwide retail category and supply chain operations teams, in-house scientists, other product managers, and software teams to define new features and products. You will analyze the potential customer and financial impacts, select the most promising ideas, prioritize them, and create a cohesive roadmap that makes the best use of available resources. You will also evangelize new features to our internal customers, working to accelerate feature adoption, track the realized impacts, and communicate results with senior leadership.

This is a highly visible role and will require regular interaction and communication with senior leaders. You must have the experience and capability to prepare documentation for senior executives and align your roadmap with Amazon’s strategic objectives. Excellent written and verbal communication skills are a necessity. Successful candidates should excel at diving into data in order to analyze problems and implement simple, long term solutions. You will have the opportunity to thrive in a highly collaborative, creative, analytical, and fast-paced environment oriented around building the world’s most flexible and effective supply chain management technology.

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager - Tech, Social Advertising
jobs.description:
Have you ever discovered a product through a creator you follow on social media, then bought it on Amazon? Do you wonder how brands find the right creators to partner with at scale?

We are building a new social advertising product that helps brands find customers on social media apps through creators. As the Principal PMT for this new product, you will own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap. You'll define how brands discover high-affinity creators, how campaigns get activated, how creators get compensated, and how the whole system integrates with Amazon's existing advertising products (DSP, Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, and Creator Ads). You need to be fluent in both worlds: how creators build audiences and monetize content on social platforms, AND how brands evaluate and buy media programmatically.

This is a 0-to-1 role. You would be building a new product from the ground up, working backwards from what brands and creators need to define how the product serves both customers and how it goes to market. If you have built creator tools, advertising products, or multi-sided marketplaces, and especially if you have done more than one of those, we want to talk.

Key job responsibilities
As a Principal Product Manager-Technical for this new product, you will be responsible for building a new product at the intersection of the creator economy and advertising technology. To thrive in this role, you will need to demonstrate:
- Bilateral Fluency: You understand both sides of the marketplace: how creators build audiences, create content, and monetize on social platforms (TikTok, Instagram, YouTube) AND how brands evaluate, buy, and measure media programmatically. You can context-switch between a conversation about creator authenticity and one about ROAS measurement without losing either thread.
- 0-to-1 Builder Instinct: You are an expert at evaluating whether to take a scrappy approach or spend the time to build a durable solution. Every wrong call here costs precious time. You have a track record of getting this right consistently in ambiguous, early-stage environments where there is no playbook to follow.
- Cross-Org Influence: This product delivers most of its value through other teams' systems. You will do significant away-team work in Ads, Associates, and external platform integrations. You earn trust from day one and maintain it through hard conversations where you push partner teams to do things they would not otherwise prioritize.
- Data-Grounded Conviction: You use data to form strong opinions, state them clearly, and update them when evidence warrants. You do not hedge conclusions the data supports, and you do not overstate conclusions it does not.
- Technical Depth: You can engage meaningfully with scientists on matching algorithms, with engineers on API design, and with ads teams on DSP integration architecture. You do not need to write the code, but you need to understand the tradeoffs well enough to make product decisions that are technically sound.

A day in the life
You start the morning reviewing creator-brand match quality metrics and slates of individual creators from yesterday's pilot cohort. A brand partner wants to understand why certain creators rank high for their category. You pull the attribution data and walk them through the quantitative signal: which creators are driving conversions for their brand, at what volume, and how that compares to their managed roster. You then shift to qualitative evaluation of the creator's content, audience fit, and brand alignment. Mid-morning, you're in a working session with the science team debating whether to weight recent conversion velocity or lifetime brand affinity more heavily in the matching algorithm. After lunch, you're drafting the integration spec for how campaigns for this new product will surface inside the DSP console, negotiating scope with the Ads PM who owns that surface. By end of day, you're reviewing creator compensation scenarios with the Associates team, making sure the economics work for the brand (willing to pay), the creator (worth their time), and Amazon (sustainable margin).

About the team
The team is a small group of applied scientists, and engineers. We work across Amazon's creator ecosystem (Associates, Influencer Program, Creator Connections) and ads platform to build something that blends the best parts of both worlds. You would be joining at the stage where there is a solid data hypothesis and brand demand, but the core product decisions are yours to guide.

- Hands-on experience managing campaigns or building features within a programmatic advertising platform (not just familiarity)

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager - Tech, Global Transportation Technology Services
jobs.description:
Amazon moves millions of packages every day through the world's largest transportation network of planes, trucks, and delivery vehicles. Before any package can be assigned to a route, someone needs to design that network - figure out which lanes exist, how much capacity each node and lane can handle, and what changes are needed as demand shifts. That's what we build.
Global Transportation Tech Services (GTTS) creates software that manages the foundation of Amazon's outbound transportation network. Your work has direct financial impact on network efficiency and directly affects whether customers get their packages on time.
Here's what we actually do: We build the platform that transportation teams use to design and change the network - from evaluating new lanes to implementing them in production. We calculate how much capacity each node and lane will have, so the network can handle the volume. We identify where capacity will fall short and alert operators before it becomes a problem. We spot packages at risk of missing delivery and give operators tools to protect them. When a hurricane hits Florida or a snowstorm shuts down highways in Germany, our systems detect the disruption, protect customers by adjusting delivery promises, and help move volume to keep packages flowing.
The challenges are real: modeling capacity across a massive global network, managing thousands of network changes safely, predicting capacity gaps weeks in advance, detecting and responding to disruptions in real-time, and keeping systems running 24/7.
We regularly build new greenfield products while also modernizing existing systems. You'll have space to explore new technologies and approaches to solve customer problems. We work with AWS services, big data processing (Spark/Scala), optimization algorithms, machine learning models, and GenAI.

Key job responsibilities
As a leader on the team, you will be expected to operate at all levels, diving deep into the details while providing strategic inputs for the product portfolio. You will be a key player in driving strategic planning, project execution, driving operational excellence, and shaping up the solutions to achieve our vision. This is your opportunity to make a big impact and make history in the world of Global Transportation!

Sellers, seeing no traction, won't commit inventory to FBA; without FBA, the delivery promise suffers, and customer demand never materializes. The flywheel that powers Amazon's marketplace doesn't start spinning on its own and someone has to build the ignition system. That is this role.

The Japan FBA team is looking for a Principal Product Manager to own New Selection Acceleration end to end: growing not just how much new selection launches on Amazon Japan, but how much of it becomes active, in-demand selection that customers discover, buy, and repeatedly return to. You will own the north-star metric for new selection success, and build the products, programs, and economic mechanisms that take a new product from first listing to sustainable flywheel at scale, across hundreds of thousands of selling partners.

This is a high-ambiguity, greenfield charter to accelerate new selection in Japan's marketplace, where customer expectations, seller behavior, and category economics differ structurally from other Amazon geographies. You will define the problem space, size the opportunity, build the multi-year strategy and investment case, and mobilize technology, science, operations, and worldwide product teams to deliver. Your work will directly shape Japan's 3-Year Plan and will be reviewed by senior leadership in Japan and worldwide.

- Own the north-star metric for new selection success. Define and drive the measure of whether new selection becomes active, in-demand selection and build the goals, reporting, and review mechanisms around it across the business

- Build products and programs that ignite the flywheel. Design, pilot, and scale mechanisms that de-risk new selection for sellers and surface it for customers: launch incentives for unproven products, demand-signal and forecasting products for zero-history selection, FBA onboarding accelerators, and discovery interventions by working with tech and science teams to productize what works

- Own the economics of new selection. Model seller proceeds, contribution profit, and inventory risk across price bands and categories; identify where fee, program, or placement interventions turn structurally unviable selection into profitable, self-sustaining selection

- Identify and unblock systemic blockers at the root. jobs.title: Sr Manager, Product Management - Tech, AI Cost Governance, AWS Insights and Optimizations
jobs.description:
We're building the future of cloud financial management, and the hardest unsolved problem in it is AI cost. Customers are moving from experimenting with generative AI to running it in production at scale. Spend is driven by tokens, model choice, inference patterns, and increasingly by agents that make their own consumption decisions. The AWS Billing organization processes millions of events per second to deliver the cost, usage, and optimization insights that power financial decisions at the world's largest enterprises. We are now extending that foundation to give customers the ability to understand, allocate, control, and optimize AI spend with the same rigor they apply to compute and storage today.

As Senior Manager, Product Management, you will own AWS's strategy for AI cost governance as a player-coach, personally driving the category-defining work while building the team that scales it. This is the highest-ambiguity, highest-leverage product space in the organization: the mechanics of tokenomics, attribution, and control for generative AI workloads are still being defined across the industry, and the decisions made here set the direction that partner service teams, enterprise customers, and eventually all industry players respond to. You will personally own the product bets that define the category, hire and develop the product managers who help you carry that ownership as it grows, and set the technical direction that other product managers across Billing and partner teams build against.

In this role, you will define what it means to govern AI spend on AWS: how cost is attributed at the token, model, and agent level; how customers allocate that cost to teams, applications, and business units; and how they set and enforce controls before spend, rather than explaining it afterward. You will write the strategy documents and PR/FAQs for the most consequential launches, run the customer conversations, and make the hard trade-off calls on scope, sequencing, and where AWS should lead versus follow — doing this work yourself on the bets that matter most, and coaching your team to take on more of it as they grow into it. You will pressure-test metering, API, and interface designs directly with engineering, and dig into consumption data and customer telemetry to understand where the real cost drivers and governance gaps are. You will own the measurement of whether these capabilities actually change customer behavior, including adoption, spend under active governance, and the degree to which cost visibility unblocks AI expansion, and build the review mechanisms — run by you and the product managers you develop — that hold the organization accountable to it.

You will make the calls on how AI cost governance extends to emerging surfaces, including foundation model inference, agentic workloads, and third-party and marketplace model consumption, and on when AWS should build new primitives versus extend existing cost management constructs. You will partner with engineering leaders, applied science leaders, and product leaders across Bedrock, AgentCore, and the broader AWS generative AI portfolio to ensure cost governance is designed in rather than retrofitted, and you will drive alignment on strategy and investment across multiple organizations without owning the teams that execute it. You will represent this product area to senior AWS leadership, enterprise CFOs and FinOps practitioners, and industry analysts, and you will shape how the market thinks about the economics of running AI in production.

This role requires deep technical judgment, comfort operating with incomplete information on problems that have no precedent, the influence to move organizations you do not control, and the discipline to both do the work yourself and develop the people who will eventually own it without you. If you are excited about defining a product category that does not yet exist — and about the fact that every enterprise scaling generative AI will eventually need what you build — this role offers the opportunity to set AWS's position on the economics of AI.

Key job responsibilities
Set the product vision and strategy for AI cost governance across internal and external customers. Own the strategy for the highest-ambiguity bets; coach your PMs to own the strategy within their scope.
Build the mechanisms your team uses to engage customers across channels and serve as the voice of the customer inside AWS.
Establish how customer feedback flows into product decisions, and use it to make the calls on where the team invests.
Own the full product lifecycle across your team's surface area, from strategic planning through tactical execution.
Partner with engineering and applied science leaders to deliver against the roadmap. Get into the technical details on the hardest architectural and agent-design trade-offs, and grow your PMs to do the same within their areas.
Define the goals, input metrics, and output metrics that measure success for the product experience.
Own the product roadmap for your area, integrating inputs from customers, engineering, science, and peer product teams. Make the prioritization calls and defend them to senior leadership.
Write and deliver the updates that go to VP and SVP audiences on the products, key launches, and strategic bets. Coach your PMs on the writing and communication skills that get their work to the same bar.
Hire, develop, and retain a high-performing PM team. Set the bar for product excellence, give direct feedback, and grow PMs into the next level.
Basic qualifications:
- 5+ years of people management experience
- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field
- Experience in people management
- Experience contributing to engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product
- Experience overseeing roadmap strategy and definition
- Experience with feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product
Preferred qualifications:
- 8+ years of successful technology products work from ideation through launch experience
- Experience delivering technology products or services in a high growth environment
- Experience shaping business strategy for technical products or services for large enterprises or partners
- Experience with cloud native technologies

We are now at an exciting inflection point. Advances in generative and agentic AI create an opportunity to fundamentally rethink how sellers operate their businesses — moving from dashboards and workflows that tell sellers what happened, toward intelligent experiences that understand their business, identify what needs attention, recommend actions and increasingly execute work on their behalf.

As the Principal PM for SmartHub, you will define this next chapter. You will own the long-term product vision and roadmap for SmartHub and lead important horizontal capabilities such as pricing that span the broader Smart Commerce portfolio.

This is a role for a product builder who enjoys solving complex platform problems, operating in ambiguity and translating emerging technology into simple products that deliver measurable customer and business impact.

Own the product vision, strategy and roadmap for SmartHub, Amazon Smart Commerce's multi-channel operations platform spanning order management, inventory, catalog, returns, warehousing and analytics.
Define how AI and agentic experiences can transform commerce operations — helping businesses move from manually operating software toward systems that understand business context, surface opportunities and risks, recommend decisions and automate repetitive work.
Reimagine high-frequency seller workflows such as order processing, inventory management, exception handling, returns and pricing to make operating across multiple sales channels dramatically simpler.
Lead horizontal product capabilities such as pricing that can create leverage across SmartHub and the broader Smart Commerce portfolio.
Develop a deep understanding of sellers ranging from emerging businesses to high-volume brands, including the operators who use SmartHub every day in warehouses and back offices.
Use customer research, product data and business insights to identify the highest-value problems and translate them into simple, scalable product experiences.
Partner deeply with engineering, science and UX teams on complex platform and AI problems, making thoughtful trade-offs across customer experience, reliability, scalability and speed.
Define and drive metrics across adoption, engagement, operational efficiency, seller experience and business impact.
Work across Amazon and external commerce ecosystems to build integrations and capabilities that allow businesses to operate seamlessly across marketplaces and D2C channels.
Influence senior leaders and partner teams across organizational boundaries to establish long-term product and technology direction.
Raise the product management bar through strong product judgment, first-principles thinking, clear written narratives and mentorship of other product leaders.

A day in the life
You might start the day speaking with a seller or warehouse operator processing thousands of orders across Amazon, Flipkart and their own website, identifying where manual work and exceptions slow them down. Later, you could work with engineers and scientists on an AI agent that detects inventory risks or automates an operational workflow, review adoption and reliability metrics with the team, and then align senior leaders on a multi-year product strategy. You will move fluidly between warehouse-floor details, customer experience, platform architecture, AI possibilities and business strategy.

Amazon Smart Commerce is building the technology infrastructure for agentic commerce that helps businesses sell and operate wherever their customers shop.

SmartHub is our multi-channel operations platform, helping sellers bring orders, inventory, catalog, returns and business insights from multiple marketplaces and D2C channels into one system. jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Technical , OMHS Software, Controls, and Science
jobs.description:
We are looking for a Senior Product Manager, Technical with a strong technical background to own our vision for the operator console that Amazon's next-generation fulfillment buildings are run on. This is a deeply technical role. You will work side by side with software development managers, science managers, and engineers, and you will push them to build better, faster, and cheaper with more capability every quarter. We are not looking for someone to ship another monitoring dashboard. We want someone who drives the team past monitoring and alarms toward a building that catches and resolves its own problems before a human ever sees them.
That ambition is concrete: move each capability up an arc from a health overview, to automated root-cause on an issue, to a recommended next best action, to directed and eventually autonomous resolution. You will own how far and how fast our equipment advances along that arc, and you will hold engineering and science to the bar that gets us there. This is also a role for someone who leads through influence. The console is built jointly across several Amazon organizations, so you will be the single product voice for how our equipment works in it, aligning partner teams you do not control and turning several groups' priorities into one coherent product. The strategy is still being written, so you will create clarity where the problem is not yet fully defined.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the product strategy, vision, and multi-quarter roadmap for how our equipment shows up in the console, and push it up the arc from monitoring toward autonomous resolution.
- Engage engineering and science leaders as a technical peer: challenge complexity estimates, weigh architecture trade-offs on their merits, and define acceptance criteria for software that runs a live building for years.
- Be the single product voice for our organization across the partner teams that co-build the console, earning alignment through shared interest rather than escalation and reconciling competing priorities into one experience.
- Own the business value case for your product, cost to run versus operational value delivered, and make build, extend, or partner calls with clear justification.
- Run customer research in live fulfillment buildings, manage deployment readiness with Operations, sequence inbound demand against committed launches, and own the post-launch health of what you ship against adoption, reliability, cost avoided, and customer satisfaction.

A day in the life
What your morning will look like if we are successful: You start with overnight telemetry across deployed sites and a class of alarm the system should have caught and cleared on its own, which becomes your next roadmap push. Mid-morning you are with your engineering lead pressure-testing whether an automated root-cause capability can hit the latency it needs at the data volume a live building throws at it, and you hold the line on the harder, better answer. After lunch you align partner-team product leaders on how their data and your equipment views coexist in one screen, then run office hours with floor technicians during a surge to see where the product still makes them think too hard. You end the day walking a deployment readiness checklist with Operations for a building commissioning next quarter. Your customers are the operators, engineers, and technicians who use your product every day in fulfillment buildings.

About the team
We are a division within Amazon Fulfillment Technology and Robotics focused on standardizing the equipment and systems that make up our first, middle, and last mile facilities. We are a passionate group of innovators, engineers, and business leaders dedicated to reducing the variability and complacency in our current logistics systems, and we thrive on collaboration, continuous learning, and a shared vision of bringing innovation and scalability back to our automation equipment.
Amazon installs a significant quantity of new buildings every year, and the historical model let each integrator use its own equipment, controls, and methods. That variability has proven hard to support and scale. Our software organization delivers the platforms, controls architecture, and AI and computer-vision capabilities that let Amazon own its industrial automation ecosystem end to end, and this console is where a building becomes legible to the people who run it, moving operations from reacting to problems toward resolving them before they surface.

- Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition
- Experience with feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product
- Experience contributing to engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager - Technical, External Services, AWS Billing
jobs.description:
We're rebuilding the AWS product catalog for an AI-native world, and this role owns both how it's defined and how it grows. You'll set the standards every AWS product follows and define the new features, packages, and add-ons that service teams bring to customers, building the machine-readable foundation that billing, cost management, and AI agents all depend on. The AWS Billing organization serves over 200 AWS services across 30+ regions, and every one needs a product definition that is structurally correct, consistently described, and rich enough for both humans and AI to reason about. This is the foundation for commercial decisions made by external customers and internal teams.

As Senior Product Manager - Technical External Services, you'll own the AWS product model end to end: the schema, governance rules, and quality standards every product conforms to, and the new product structures service teams build on top of them. You'll define what attributes a product carries from creation, how to create standard models for different types of services (from compute and storage to AI inference and developer tools), how products relate to and compose with one another in packages and shared commercial experiences, and how the catalog enables AI agents to discover, compare, and act on products programmatically. You'll also extend the catalog with new product features, packages, and add-ons that service teams can adopt through configuration rather than custom engineering. Your work directly determines how AWS services launch and grow their products.

In this role, you'll architect the data model that underlies AWS commerce, define the governance framework that enforces it across hundreds of service teams, and establish the lifecycle and relationship standards that let products evolve and work consistently across commercial channels. You'll conduct direct research with service teams and internal consumers of product data to understand where definitions break down, translating those insights into schema improvements and governance rules. You'll work at the intersection of data architecture, billing infrastructure, and AI-native product design, defining how AWS products present themselves to the next generation of consumers.

You'll collaborate with engineering teams across AWS's billing, metering, and cost management organizations. This role requires deep technical fluency in data modeling, schema design, and systems thinking, combined with the product instinct to know which standards matter and which create bureaucracy.

If you're excited about defining the foundational data layer that makes AWS's commerce systems work this role offers the chance to shape how every AWS product is defined, described, and used across AWS commerce.

Key job responsibilities

- Extend the catalog with new product features, packages, and add-ons that service teams can adopt through configuration

jobs.title: Sr. Product Manager, Electrification Technology, GFP Electrification & Infrastructure
jobs.description:
We are looking for a Senior Product Manager - Technical who will own the business requirements for our electrification infrastructure products — everything beyond the charger itself. This is not a desk-only role. You will be in the field, deep-diving real telemetry and failure data from our deployed electrical infrastructure, then working backwards from our customers — operations teams, maintenance technicians, commissioning agents, and third-party service providers — to define, build, and scale the next generation of infrastructure equipment and monitoring solutions.
You will serve as the critical link between what our field users experience and what gets built into our infrastructure roadmap. You will translate operational pain points, maintenance friction, and commissioning challenges into clear product requirements, monitoring capabilities, and software features that make our electrification systems more reliable, observable, and self-sustaining at scale.
This role requires a product leader who is deeply technical in industrial-scale electrical systems and power electronics, while remaining relentlessly customer-obsessed. You must understand power conversion technologies (including emerging platforms like solid-state transformers), SCADA architectures, and the monitoring/telemetry pipelines that move data from field equipment to backend services. You will assess new technologies, structure pilots, gather structured feedback from field users, and evaluate third-party supplier capabilities to inform build-vs-buy decisions.
You will work cross-functionally with Systems Engineering, Hardware Engineering, Design/Deployment, Commissioning, Maintenance, Supply Chain, and our third-party equipment suppliers. You will coordinate daily with these partners and travel to sites to validate assumptions, run user testing on monitoring systems, and build relationships with the field teams whose feedback drives your roadmap.

Key job responsibilities
• Own the business requirements for all electrification infrastructure products excluding the charger itself, including power distribution equipment, switchgear, transformers, power conversion equipment, and associated monitoring systems
• Deep dive field data on current electrical infrastructure issues to identify product gaps, prioritize investments, and build the business case for monitoring, telemetry, and equipment improvements
• Work backwards from operations, maintenance personnel, commissioning agents, and third-party technicians to define scalable infrastructure solutions that grow with Amazon's electrification program
• Build and coordinate user testing programs for monitoring systems, ensuring field usability, data quality, and alignment with customer workflows
• Assess emerging power conversion technologies (e.g., solid-state transformers) and structure pilots to validate performance, reliability, and operational fit; own feedback collection and go/no-go recommendations
• Evaluate third-party supplier capabilities and drive supplier selection, roadmap alignment, and technical requirement negotiations
• Own the product roadmap for software features supporting infrastructure resiliency, including auto-healing capabilities that maintain system uptime through single power-module failures
• Define requirements for SCADA integration and telemetry pipelines that transmit field data to backend services for analytics, alerting, and predictive maintenance
• Feed prioritized, well-defined requirements into Systems Engineering and coordinate daily with third-party suppliers, Supply Chain, Design/Deployment, Commissioning, and Maintenance teams
• Represent the voice of the customer in design reviews, supplier business reviews, and program milestone reviews

A day in the life
Your morning starts reviewing overnight telemetry from deployed sites — you're deep-diving a pattern of power module derating events across three sites to determine whether it's a design gap or an installation issue, and the data will feed directly into a PRFAQ you're drafting for a next-gen monitoring feature. By midday, you're on a call with a commissioning agent walking through friction points in the current field diagnostics workflow — insights that will shape user acceptance criteria for the monitoring UI your team is piloting next quarter.
Later in the week, you lead a working session with a solid-state transformer supplier to assess their product roadmap against your requirements, then meet with Systems Engineering to hand off requirements for a redundancy feature. Between customer interviews and supplier deep-dives, you're building something bigger: a monitoring platform strategy that scales with Amazon's electrification footprint. You close the week presenting your product roadmap, pilot results, and customer feedback synthesis to your director.

About the team
Global Fleet and Products, Electrification and Infrastructure is building the backbone of Amazon's electric vehicle future. We are responsible for designing, deploying, and sustaining all electrification infrastructure globally to support Amazon's logistics EV fleet — one of the largest commercial electric vehicle deployments globally.
We operate at the intersection of electrical engineering, construction, fleet operations, and technology — delivering infrastructure that must perform reliably at massive scale, in diverse environments, under demanding operational conditions. Our work directly enables Amazon's Climate Pledge commitment and powers the vehicles that deliver to customers' doorsteps every day.
This is a team where product managers solve real, tangible problems. If you're energized by defining products that deploy complex electrical systems at unprecedented scale and obsessed with working backwards from field users to make them work flawlessly, this is where you belong.
Basic qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree
- Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition
- Experience with feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product
- Experience contributing to engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product
- Experience managing technical products or online services
- Experience in representing and advocating for a variety of critical customers and stakeholders during executive-level prioritization and planning
- Bachelor's degree in a quantitative/technical field such as computer science, engineering, statistics
- •3+ years of experience with industrial-scale electrical systems, power electronics, power distribution, or electrification infrastructure (e.g., solar/energy storatge, utility interconnections, switchgear, transformers, power conversion equipment)
Preferred qualifications:

- • Experience structuring technology pilots, assessing third-party supplier capabilities, and driving build-vs-buy decisions

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager - Technical, External Services, AWS, GenAIUX
jobs.description:
The AWS CX GenAIUX team is building intelligent, personalized experiences that meet users where they are. We believe that different personas—builders, operators, decision-makers, learners—deserve purpose-built GenAI applications tailored to their workflows, mental models, and goals. We are a fast-moving team that values customer obsession, bias for action, and thinking big. We believe that our customers need not to learn AWS, rather we should learn customer’s and enable them to build on AWS wherever and however they prefer. We follow their intent and help them build.
Our team sits at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence and User Experience — Our vision is to cater to the need of every personality of the customers, define the future of persona driven applications and democratizing innovation for all customers on earth. We believe that different personas — builders, operators, decision-makers, and learners — deserve purpose-built GenAI applications tailored to their workflows, mental models, and goals. We measure success trust earned, adoption of applications and enhancing the AWS adoption.

We're building the future of how people and AI work together on cloud infrastructure, and this role is central to that vision.
ABOUT THE ROLE

Model a "builder PM" culture where hands-on experimentation is the norm, not the exception.
We are seeking a Principal Product Manager - Technical to define the ever-evolving persona strategy for AWS's GenAI-powered customer applications, establish the application frameworks that translate persona insights into a portfolio of applications, and drive flywheel for success of our customers at AWS.
This requires a person who can drive a vision with conviction, remain stub-born on the vision yet flexible on the journey. This is a usability problem as much as a technology problem. The challenge is envisioning product for differentiated experiences where each customer intuitively understands the GenAI applications to leverage, trusts them enough to integrate into their life, delegate progressively complex work, and feels in control throughout. You will define how different customer personas experience trust, autonomy, and transparency differently — and translate that into distinct product experiences.
organization-level alignment on what we build, for whom, and why.

This is not a "strategy-only" role. In the era of Generative AI, the most impactful product leaders are hands-on builders who prototype before they prescribe, validate with working artifacts before writing documents, and earn engineering credibility by building alongside their teams. We expect you to be fluent in the tools and technologies you're shaping — capable of prompting, prototyping, and evaluating GenAI systems firsthand (a hands-on builder).

This is a high-ambiguity, high-impact opportunity to make a difference in AWS customer’s life with technology revolution. The problem space is largely undefined: we do not yet have a systematic understanding of how millions of AWS users (both tech and non-tech), e.g. from junior developers to C-suite executives should experience AI-native workflows differently. You will define the strategy, build the mechanisms, set the direction that an experienced engineering team executes against, and personally validate critical bets through hands-on prototyping. You will operate with significant independence, and influencing leadership, roadmap decisions across AWS CX with laser focus on Customers.

Key job responsibilities
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Persona Strategy & Frameworks (Org-Level)
• Define and own the persona strategy for AWS GenAI experiences — establishing a scalable, data-driven framework that the broader organization uses to segment, prioritize, and serve differentiated customer cohorts
• Set the methodology for persona research (qualitative and quantitative), and direct L5/L6 PMs, UX researchers, and data scientists who execute against it
• Establish a living persona framework that becomes an organizational asset — referenced in OP1/OP2 planning, used by engineering to make architecture decisions, and adopted by adjacent AWS teams
Portfolio Strategy & Application Definition
• Translate persona insights into a portfolio of GenAI application concepts, defining the investment thesis for each: target persona, differentiated value, technical moat, and business model
• Own the "working backwards" narrative at the portfolio level — authoring L7-grade PR/FAQs that articulate the 3-year vision and secure L8–L10 sponsorship. Supplement narratives with functional prototypes that make the vision tangible.
• Make hard prioritization decisions across competing application investments, using a rigorous framework that balances customer impact, technical feasibility, time-to-value, and strategic positioning
Product Roadmap & Org-Level Alignment
• Define success metrics grounded in customer outcomes — adoption by persona, task completion rates, trust signals (autonomy granted over time), friction reduction, and retention — with clear input/output metric trees that teams can decompose and own
• Identify and escalate strategic trade-offs to senior leadership with clear recommendations
Cross-Functional & External Leadership
• Influence senior leadership (L8–L10) with compelling, data-backed narratives that shape organizational priorities and resource allocation
• Drive cross-org partnerships (Console, Documentation, Well-Architected, Training & Certification) to ensure persona insights are leveraged broadly
• Represent AWS externally — customer advisory boards, re:Invent sessions, whitepapers, live demos — as the thought leader on persona-driven GenAI experiences
• Engage directly with external AWS customers to understand their workflows, observe how they interact with agent experiences across personas, and ensure design decisions are grounded in real behavior
• Attract, mentor, and develop PM talent; raise the product management bar across the team. Model a "builder PM" culture where hands-on experimentation is the norm, not the exception.
BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

• 4+ years of technical experience (software development, ML/AI systems, or other hands-on engineering work)
• 10+ years of technical product management, program management, or engineering experience, with at least 5 years at a senior/principal level owning portfolio-level strategy
• Experience delivering large-scale products where you are responsible for the full product lifecycle, from concept through launch
• Experience building complex software systems that have been successfully delivered to customers
• Demonstrated experience shipping AI/ML or Generative AI products at scale
• Hands-on experience building with GenAI tooling — evidence of personal prototyping, prompt engineering, or building functional demos/POCs (not just writing requirements for others to build)
• Proven ability to operate in high-ambiguity environments — defining both the problem and the solution where neither is well-understood
• Track record of influencing org-level strategy and driving alignment across multiple teams (engineering, science, design, business)
• Experience establishing mechanisms and frameworks adopted beyond your immediate team
• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field (or equivalent experience)
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

The Opportunity

What if you could teach machines to make millions of delivery decisions — faster, smarter, and more efficiently than ever before? We're looking for a Senior Product Manager - Tech who's obsessed with the intersection of artificial intelligence and real-world operations to join Amazon's Sub Same Day team. This isn't about incremental optimization. This is about building intelligent systems that autonomously orchestrate one of the most complex delivery networks on the planet — in real time, at massive scale.

You will define and drive the product roadmap for AI/ML-powered solutions across the Sub Same Day delivery network — from supply chain planning and real-time capacity allocation to delivery and anomaly detection. You'll identify high-impact business problems ripe for AI disruption, translate them into well-scoped technical product requirements, and build the business case to secure investment. Your multi-year product vision will leverage state-of-the-art techniques — large language models, reinforcement learning, computer vision, and graph neural networks — to fundamentally reimagine how last-mile delivery works at Amazon scale.

You will serve as the connective tissue between data scientists, system development engineers, business intelligence engineers — ensuring technical feasibility, architectural soundness, and delivery velocity. You'll own the end-to-end product lifecycle: from problem framing and data pipeline design through model development, A/B experimentation, production deployment, and continuous iteration. This means making hard trade-off decisions across model accuracy, latency, infrastructure cost, and customer experience — with a deep understanding of the technical constraints and opportunities. You'll drive technical debt reduction and platform scalability, ensuring AI systems are production-grade, fault-tolerant, and built for exponential growth.

You will partner with operations, logistics, finance, and science teams to ensure AI solutions are grounded in operational reality and deliver measurable business value. You'll influence senior leadership with data-driven narratives, translating complex ML concepts into clear strategic recommendations, and build scalable processes for feature prioritization, sprint planning, and release management across distributed engineering teams.

What Makes This Role Different

Your AI products will make decisions affecting millions of packages daily across Amazon's fastest-growing delivery channel. You'll work with large-scale ML platforms (SageMaker, custom training infrastructure), and production inference systems operating at sub-100ms latency. Sub Same Day is still early in its AI journey — you'll have the rare opportunity to define the foundational AI strategy from the ground up, not just optimize existing systems. From the data that feeds models to the customer experience those models create — you own the full stack of outcomes.

Alexa Smart Properties enables enterprise customers to deploy Alexa in their managed properties like hotels, senior living homes, vacation rentals, hospitals, and more, transforming how businesses engage with their customers and streamline staff processes. Come join us to invent the future of how millions of enterprise end users communicate and connect through Alexa-powered devices — and how businesses manage those experiences at scale.

As a Senior Product Manager — Technical in Alexa Smart Properties, you will own and drive the product vision and execution for our enterprise staff personas to make it easy for staff to manage their content, get real time insights, and engage with their end customers. You will own our enterprise console and integrations with third party systems. jobs.description:
In the Worldwide Returns & ReCommerce (WW R&R) group at Amazon, we are dedicated to ‘making zero happen’ – zero cost of returns, zero waste, and zero defects – to benefit our customers, company, and environment. We are an agile and inclusive organization that constantly innovates to create long-term value by investing in our people and our planet, not simply focusing on the bottom line.

WW R&R includes business, product, operations, data, and software engineering teams, who together manage the lifecycle of returned and damaged products. In WW R&R, you will partner across these teams to help customers get the most value out of Amazon’s products; improve the customer returns experience; and reduce defects, waste, and cost in reverse logistics processes. You will be a leader, a builder, and an owner, collaborating cross-functionally with technical, operations, and business teams to design scalable and automated solutions to customer problems.

Evaluation Automation charter is dedicated to grading every returned item with machine-learned precision instead of static rules, by building the science based scalable solutions that replace heuristic rules for sellability and recovery disposition thereby maximizing sellable yield, reducing associate subjectivity, and protecting the customer experience across Amazon's reverse logistics network.

We're looking for someone who has a passion for working in cross functional environment, strong communication skills (verbal & written) in addition to proven product management experience. Join us if you want the opportunity to make a big impact in a quickly growing team that can make a big difference in the customers' journey with Amazon.

Amazon is Earth’s most customer-centric company and in WW R&R, the Earth is our customer too. Come join us and innovate with the Amazon Worldwide Returns & ReCommerce.

jobs.title: Product Manager III - Tech, Reputation Marketing & Insights
jobs.description:
The individual selected for this position will own the product strategy, roadmap, and delivery of RMI's survey measurement platform — the system that determines how hundreds of millions of dollars in reputation marketing investment are defined, measured, and optimized.

The work will challenge you to be resourceful, think big while staying connected to the details, translate complex research requirements into scalable technical solutions, and embrace a high degree of change and ambiguity at speed. The scope and scale of what we strive to achieve is immense, but it is also meaningful and energizing.

Key job responsibilities
Reputation Marketing & Insights (RMI) is hiring a Product Manager - Technical to define the product and technology strategy for the team's measurement capability. You will own the full lifecycle of survey-based measurement products — from audience definition and instrument design through data integration, analysis infrastructure, and stakeholder-facing outputs. Product strategy, methodology, technology approach, and vendor relationships are yours to define. You will deliver independently with limited guidance.

Working with media, data science, public policy, and creative teams — as well as external research agency partners — you will identify where manual research processes create drag and define product solutions that scale. You will architect the system that connects survey instruments to operational data — media delivery logs, audience segment behavior, earned media signals, and programmatic outcomes — to explain why survey results move, not merely that they moved. You will evaluate and leverage AI/ML tools, large language models, and agentic frameworks to accelerate research workflows, improve analytical depth, and reduce dependency on manual vendor processes. You will define technical requirements — including survey instrument APIs, data integrations, attribution frameworks, and cloud architecture — and articulate when a new technology is needed (and when it is not). You will manage external research agency partnerships end-to-end, owning the long-term build-vs-buy roadmap for which measurement capabilities remain outsourced versus built internally. You will be accountable for measurement product quality, methodological rigor, research operations uptime, and strategic relevance.

A day in the life
You will define product strategy and own the full lifecycle for a portfolio of measurement products — from survey instrument design through deployment of scalable research infrastructure. You'll build audience segmentation methodology that determines who belongs in the persuasion target and how to reach them through paid channels. You'll run your own crosstabs and statistical tests against weighted survey data, translating findings into recommendations that reallocate spend or adjust targeting. You'll define the operational handoff between campaign execution and measurement systems. You'll evaluate emerging AI capabilities for automating research workflows with agency vendors. You'll navigate a volatile environment where public affairs issues shift faster than annual research cycles accommodate — adapting methodology on the fly.

About the team
Our team strives to identify the persuasive return on investment for every dollar we spend. We build marketing plans that persuade our core audiences through best-in-class media tactics and measurement methodology that enables us to optimize towards the principles and platforms that achieve real-world outcomes at the expense of those that don't.

Our team is dedicated to supporting new members. We have a broad mix of experience levels and tenures, and we're building an environment that celebrates knowledge sharing and mentorship. We care about your career growth and strive to assign projects based on what will help each team member develop into a better-rounded professional and enable them to take on more complex tasks in the future.

jobs.description:
Ring & Blink Products & Delivery Org is looking for a Technical Program Manager (TPM) to own end-to-end hardware product development for our accessory portfolio — gateways, battery packs, solar chargers, power supplies, mounting kits, installation hardware, and other peripherals that enable millions of Ring and Blink devices to deliver on their most popular customer use cases.

You will drive programs from concept through mass production, partnering with cross-functional engineering teams, contract manufacturers (CMs) and ODMs in Asia, and US-based product and engineering stakeholders. As the single-threaded owner for accessory program execution, you are accountable for on-time delivery, quality, and cost targets.

At Ring/Blink, TPMs operate with AI-native fluency — leveraging AI tools as a core part of how you plan, execute, communicate, and deliver. AI fluency that doesn't improve customer outcomes is not sufficient; you own every output you ship, AI-assisted or not.

Key job responsibilities
- Program Ownership: Own end-to-end accessory development from concept all the way to launch through sustaining/EOL.
- Schedule & Risk Management: Build and maintain workback schedules; identify critical-path risks and drive mitigations with data-backed recommendations — escalate with options, not just problems.
- Cross-Functional Coordination: Drive aligned execution across PM, ID, ME, EE, FW, Quality, Compliance, Operations, and Supply Chain.
- CM/ODM Management: Serve as primary TPM interface with Asia-based manufacturing partners. Lead build readiness reviews, tooling schedules, and production issue resolution. Travel to sites (China/Vietnam) for key builds as needed.
- Technical Depth: Maintain sufficient hardware design fluency (ME, EE, materials) to identify risks early and facilitate engineering trade-offs within program constraints.
- BOM & Cost: Track BOM convergence and drive cost-down through component selection, 2nd-source qualification, and process optimization to meet guardrail targets.
- Stakeholder Communication: Deliver regular program health updates to leadership covering status, decisions, and change-control items.
- AI-Native Practice: Design workflows with AI embedded from the start — automated status generation, risk detection, data synthesis, and reusable tooling (reports, scorecards, dependency tracking) that the team adopts. Actively develop expertise in at least one AI domain relevant to TPM work.

A day in the life
You own 2–4 accessory programs at various development stages. In a typical week you're reviewing tooling status with the CM, running a cross-functional build-readiness review for an upcoming DVT build, using AI-generated portfolio dashboards to identify at-risk milestones, driving an open-issue list with EE/ME engineers to closure, and preparing a milestone-gate read-out for leadership. You balance hands-on execution with forward-looking planning — and you're continuously looking for ways to automate the routine so you can focus on decisions and strategy.

About the team
The Ring & Blink Accessories HW TPM team is part of the broader Ring & Blink Products & Delivery Org. We develop the full range of accessory products — from gateways, battery packs and solar panels to corner kits, wedge kits, and installation hardware — that complement our camera, doorbell, and alarm product lines. Our team operates in Taipei, working closely with engineering in the US and Taiwan and manufacturing partners across Asia to deliver high-quality, cost-effective accessories at scale.

jobs.description:
It’s no secret that Amazon relies on its technology to deliver millions of packages every day to its customers – on time, with low cost. The Middle Mile technology organization, builds complex software solutions that work across our vendors, warehouses and carriers to optimize both time & cost of getting the packages delivered. Our services already handle thousands of requests per second, make business decisions impacting billions of dollars a year, integrate with a network of small and large carriers, owner operators and drivers worldwide, manage business rules for millions of unique products, and improve ordering and delivery experience for millions of online shoppers. That said, this remains a fast growing business and our technical journey has only started. An example of a recent innovation from this group is AmazonFlex (flex.amazon.com) that enables crowdsourced last mile delivery. With rapid expansion into new geographies, innovations in supply chain, unique delivery models for products ranging from AmazonFresh groceries, ultra-fast Prime Now deliveries to big-screen TV’s, increasingly complex transportation network, and growing number of shipments worldwide, we see a brand new opportunity to fundamentally change the way people get the stuff they need, and make a big impact by cutting billions of dollars of transportation costs from the ecosystem. Our mission is to build the most efficient and optimal transportation solution on the planet, using our technology and engineering muscle as our biggest advantage. We aim to leverage technologies in big data, machine learning, and optimization techniques, and operate high volume, low latency, and high availability services. Oh, and we will need great leaders too (this is where you come in … read on)

As a member of this collaborative team, you will have an opportunity to make an impact in Amazon Logistics and work with a group of talented program managers, product managers, research scientists, software developers, and business stakeholders to design the Amazon network of the future.

As a Sr. Product Manager, you will operate at the crossroads of multiple complex Amazon systems, getting global visibility of how Amazon moves inventory across out network and serves our customers. Specifically, this role will be responsible for driving the delivery of technology features that enable our real time routing technology. This role will also own critical efficiency metrics that measure how well we utilize our capacity, where we have opportunities to expand, and how can we better manager our P&L. As a business owner you will be expected to monitor weekly metrics and callouts, direct and occasionally perform deep dives, generate product artifacts (vision and strategy documents, BRD, Launch Plans), and contribute to monthly business reviews with VPs.

The successful candidate will be voraciously curious about Amazon’s transportation operations and how data consumed and produced by our systems can be used to improve outcomes and lower costs. Your responsibility is to expose and measure the current performance of our systems, find and quantify opportunities for improvement, and dive deep into existing algorithms to explain unexpected performance. 3. Communicate and collaborate cross-functionally across multiple teams in operations, technology and planning to define strategic roadmaps while keeping the impact of the solution to all stakeholders in mind

5. Designing and implementing feedback mechanisms to drive performance and cost improvement in processes

jobs.title: Sr. Product Manager - Technical, Responsible AI
jobs.description:
AI is transforming every corner of Amazon — and with that transformation comes the responsibility to get it right. The Amazon Responsible AI (RAI) team is building the systems and programs that ensure Amazon's AI is fair, safe, transparent, and compliant with emerging global regulations. We are looking for a Sr. Product Manager - Technical who wants to define the product vision for AI governance at Amazon scale — building the tools and experiences that help thousands of builder teams develop AI responsibly without slowing down.

No one has solved AI governance at this scale before. Today, tracking thousands of AI systems against evolving regulatory frameworks, internal expectations, and voluntary commitments is a problem that's impossible to manage manually. You'll define the product that makes it possible — automating what would take an army of auditors, and giving builders the tools to do the right thing without slowing down. This is a greenfield opportunity on a small, senior team building from scratch alongside Amazon Scholars, Principal Applied Scientists, and policy experts. You'll own the product vision and shape the platform direction.

As a PMT on the Responsible AI team, you will define and drive the product strategy for our AI governance platform, working at the intersection of technology, policy, and science. You'll partner deeply with engineering teams building the platform, Applied Scientists developing AI-powered classification and assessment models, and policy experts interpreting regulatory requirements — turning ambiguity into a clear, prioritized roadmap that delivers customer value.

This role is for product leaders who thrive in ambiguity, are energized by the challenge of defining new product categories, and are motivated by the societal impact of ensuring AI systems are developed responsibly.

Key job responsibilities
- Define the product vision, strategy, and multi-year roadmap for Amazon's AI governance platform — the system that provides portfolio-level visibility into AI compliance posture across the company
- Own the end-to-end product lifecycle for responsible AI tooling: from discovery and customer research through requirements definition, development, launch, and adoption at scale
- Translate complex regulatory requirements (EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, emerging state/federal AI legislation) and internal responsible AI expectations into builder-friendly product experiences and self-service workflows
- Drive product strategy for AI system discovery, risk classification, and compliance evidence collection — working backward from builder needs to reduce friction while meeting governance obligations
- Define metrics and KPIs that measure responsible AI adoption, tool effectiveness, and compliance coverage — using data to prioritize roadmap investments and communicate progress to leadership

- Work cross-functionally with Privacy, Legal, Security, and RAI Science to ensure product decisions align with regulatory obligations, customer trust requirements, and scientific best practices
- Influence engineering architecture decisions by evaluating technical trade-offs, understanding system constraints, and ensuring the platform can scale to support Amazon's AI portfolio
- Develop and present product strategy, roadmaps, and business cases to VP+ leadership — clearly articulating the value proposition and investment rationale for responsible AI tooling

About the team
Amazon Responsible AI works to maximize the benefits and minimize the risks of AI technology across Amazon. We define responsible AI through core dimensions — Fairness, Safety, Privacy, Security, Veracity, Robustness, Explainability, Transparency, Controllability, and Governance — and we build the tools and programs that help Amazon's builder teams deliver on those dimensions at scale. Our team includes Applied Scientists, Amazon Scholars, Security Engineers, TPMs, SDEs, and policy specialists. We are science-led, independent advisors who prioritize enablement over enforcement — providing expert guidance and practical solutions that make responsible AI easy to implement. We are building the next generation of AI governance infrastructure from the ground up.
