jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
Annapurna Labs designs the custom silicon that powers AWS's machine learning infrastructure, including the Trainium and Inferentia chip families. Our next-generation ML accelerator is a multi-die chiplet using state-of-the-art packaging technology, and it is the most complex hardware program Amazon has undertaken. We are looking for a Principal Technical Program Manager to own end-to-end program execution for this chip, from RTL freeze through tape-out and into production readiness.

This is not a status-reporting role. You will be the person who connects a sprawling set of engineering workstreams into a single coherent schedule, identifies the real critical path week to week, and drives the cross-functional decisions that keep the program on track. The program spans multiple concurrent silicon development efforts with significant interdependencies across engineering disciplines, external partners, and infrastructure.

Key job responsibilities
Own the integrated schedule and critical path analysis across multiple die tape-outs through engineering samples and production ramp. Understand dependency chains deeply enough to calculate the impact of any slip or pull-in, and update the timeline weekly with real data.
Drive the weekly chip status cadence by synthesizing inputs from RTL/DV, physical design, packaging, power, infrastructure, and post-silicon teams into a single view that tells leadership where we actually stand, including what is getting worse and what needs action.
Track verification convergence as a leading indicator by monitoring the progression from feature completion through RTL closure, bug trends, and regression pass rates by block. Recognize when convergence is stalling and drive the engineering response before downstream milestones are affected.
Manage the external design partner interface, owning the netlist delivery calendar, tracking your partner's physical design timeline, and negotiating schedule trades with a clear understanding of downstream cost.
Drive infrastructure readiness and external IP delivery by partnering with compute and EDA platform teams on capacity planning, and tracking third-party PHY, memory interface, and controller IP deliveries against consuming blocks to escalate gaps before they become tape-out critical.

A day in the life
You start your morning reviewing verification convergence dashboards and regression results, spotting a block where bug closure rates haven't flattened. You pull the DV lead and RTL owner into a quick sync to agree on a recovery plan before the weekly chip status review. In that review, you walk leadership through an updated critical path that reflects a netlist delivery shift from your external design partner, quantifying the downstream impact on tape-out timing. After lunch, you join an infrastructure capacity review to confirm that compute clusters can handle the regression load through freeze, then close out the day preparing an executive summary for an upcoming program milestone review.

About the team
The Annapurna Labs ML Accelerator team builds the Trainium and Inferentia silicon that trains and serves machine learning models across AWS. We work at the intersection of chip architecture, physical design, verification, and infrastructure to deliver products that push the boundaries of performance and efficiency for our customers. Our team values people who bring strong technical judgment, clear communication, and a willingness to get into the details. If you want to shape how Amazon builds its most ambitious hardware and work alongside talented engineers solving real problems at scale, this is the role for you.
Basic qualifications:
- 10+ years of hands-on work managing complex technology projects experience
- 10+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
- Deep working knowledge of the chip development lifecycle: RTL verification milestones, physical design convergence, DFT, and timing closure.
- Experience managing programs with external design partners and IP vendors where you don't control the resources but own the outcome.
- Demonstrated ability to build and maintain integrated schedules with real dependency modeling — not just Gantt charts, but an understanding of which paths have float and which don't.
- Strong technical communication skills: ability to present crisp status to VP-level audiences, distinguishing signal from noise, and framing decisions clearly.
Preferred qualifications:
- Experience with multi-die / chiplet / advanced packaging programs (2.5D/3D integration).
- Familiarity with HBM integration, die-to-die interfaces, or high-speed serial subsystems.
- Experience with leading-edge foundry nodes and their specific flow and schedule characteristics.
- Background in ML accelerator or high-performance compute silicon.
- Experience driving infrastructure capacity planning for large-scale chip development programs.

jobs.description:
In Annapurna Labs we are at the forefront of hardware/software accelerator solutions for not only Amazon Web Services (AWS), but across the industry. The Annapurna AI Systems team owns design, validation, deployment, manufacturing, quality, reliability and fleet operations end to end.
Turning the silicon and systems into serving capacity is a manufacturing problem at a scale and pace the industry has not run before: cards, boards, sleds and servers built into racks across a global manufacturing footprint, then shipped to globally diverse datacenters and converted into capacity customers can launch on.

The Trainium Manufacturing, Quality and Reliability team owns that path end to end, and we looking for candidates interested in diving deep into our manufacturing, scaling and quality processes to support current and future generations of accelerator silicon/systems.

You will be responsible for managing server and rack manufacturing programs across our North America footprint — build plan attainment, rolled-through yield, test cycle time, work-in-process health and on-time shipment to datacenter — at ODM and CM sites.

We are seeking an experienced TPM who is equally comfortable on a factory floor and in a data set. You will reconcile what a partner reports, what the test data says, and what the design actually permits — and then drive the plan that closes the gap. Come join us!

Key job responsibilities
- You will own manufacturing programs end to end across our ODM and CM partners: build rate against plan, rolled-through yield, first-pass test cycle time, aged work-in-process, and on-time shipment to datacenter.
- You will establish the operating cadence with each partner — weekly build and recovery reviews, clear commitments, and an escalation path into vendor leadership that you are trusted to use.
- You will own material readiness, operational support and constraint resolution — critical component supply, mechanical and enclosure quality, and staging capacity at each site. The job is to identify the constraint before it caps the build rate, and to drive the cross-functional plan that clears it.
- You will drive manufacturing readiness for new rack platforms, defining entry and exit criteria for each build phase and gating ramp decisions on demonstrated yield and cycle time rather than on schedule pressure.
- You will coordinate across Design Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Manufacturing Test, Quality and Reliability, Supply Chain, Global Supplier Management, Logistics and EC2. Manufacturing sits between design intent and deployed capacity.
- You will build the reporting layer — define the metrics that describe manufacturing health, automate them where you can, and give senior leadership a clear weekly position on what shipped, what is at risk, what you need and by when.

You will work independently in a dynamic, challenging, and fast-changing organization. We’re changing an industry, and we need individuals who are ready for this challenge and who want to reach beyond what is possible today.

A day in the life
Your day to day responsibilities will include interfacing with our engineering teams, vendors and customers to understand project requirements and facilitate manufacturing output and scaling . You will work directly with vendors and ODM/JDM/CM teams to develop and manufacture your product at scale.

You will review build, yield and ship numbers from each site against plan and determine key bottlenecks and engage the right teams to overcome them. You will lead output and recovery reviews with ODM/CM leadership, pushing back on a commitment you do not believe the line can hold and landing on a number you can both defend. You will coordinate with vendor and Amazon supply chain teams to align materials with your build plans. You will write daily/weekly reports as necessary to inform leadership on the current state and key challenges.

About the team
Our team is dedicated to supporting new members. We have a broad mix of experience levels and tenures, and we’re building an environment that celebrates knowledge-sharing and mentorship. Our senior members enjoy one-on-one mentoring and thorough reviews. We care about your career growth and strive to assign projects that help our team members develop your engineering expertise so you feel empowered to take on more complex tasks in the future. We care about growing the people on this team — the work is genuinely hard, the feedback is direct and kind, and nobody here is short of problems worth solving.

jobs.description:
Unified Authorization is responsible for securing customer and corporate communication across all of Amazon. Whether it's the retail website, Alexa, or Kindle, we ensure actors are authenticated and authorized to take the requested action. Every aspect of Amazon's business interacts with our systems, including enabling the next generation of retail services on AWS infrastructure. As a global security provider, we're at the intersection of resiliency, availability, and the need to move at agile internet speed.

You are an experienced technical program manager who can work closely with product management and other business partners to define strategy and requirements, and help lead teams from concept through delivery and subsequent operation. You have regular communication with senior management on status, risks and product strategy. You have excellent listening, writing skills and very strong technical competency. Last but not the least; you have a high bar for quality and passion for design and architecture.

As the ideal candidate you will be experienced in working closely with a team of software development engineers and have a proven track record of working on complex software solutions using an agile methodology. You will have the ability to dive deep into the understanding of problems in order to help your team make the right decisions for the product and the business. You will have a proven track record of working across organizational lines. You will also be a strong communicator and will have proven abilities in managing through ambiguous situations.

About the team
Unified Auth is responsible for securing every service transaction within Amazon SDO’s service-oriented architecture (SOA) by authenticating the services involved in the transaction, authorizing APIs access, and enforcing least-privilege access to Amazon’s business data such as Cart, Order, Customer Identity, Item, Employee Information and more. Unified Auth’s systems are classified as Maximally Secure Applications (MSA) by Amazon Security as they control access to all Amazon services. Amazon’s SOA is large, complex, and ever-growing. A single Amazon customer interaction such as adding an item into cart, proceeding to checkout, adding/changing payment methods, confirming purchase, etc. spans tens to hundreds of inter-service interactions that must be secured and observed using Unified Auth’s systems. Stores, Alexa, Ring, IMDB, Prime Video, Advertisement, Selling Partners, Pharmacy, Ordering and Payments, Fulfillment Centers, and Amazon’s internal systems such as PXT rely on Unified Auth solutions to meet rising access control security and privacy standards, such as Digital Markets Act (DMA) compliance, GDPR, and SOC 2 Type II certification.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Technical Program Management, Creative Experiences & Retail Ad Server
jobs.description:
Amazon Advertising is one of Amazon’s fastest growing businesses, delivering hundreds of billions of ad impressions across 50+ countries to help advertisers reach customers wherever they shop, stream, and browse. Within Amazon Ads, the Creative Experience (CRX) and Retail Ad Services (RAS) organizations own the systems and programs that determine what ad creatives consumers see, how those creatives are assembled in real time, and how retail advertising demand reaches audiences at global scale.

We are looking for a Sr. Manager, Technical Program Management to lead a team of TPMs who drive execution across CRX and RAS. You will own the program management function for two interconnected organizations: CRX, which builds the AI-powered creative generation, optimization, and serving systems behind every display, video, and audio ad rendered across Amazon surfaces; and RAS, which manages the retailer advertising platform enabling first-party and third-party demand to flow through Amazon’s ad exchange infrastructure.

In this role, you will manage a team of TPMs spanning four program areas: Advertiser Experience (AX), Universal Creative (UC), Creative Brain (CB), and Retail Ad Services (RAS). Your team will drive multi-quarter programs across generative AI creative pipelines, real-time ad assembly systems, multi-armed bandit optimization frameworks, and retailer advertising integrations. You will partner directly with engineering directors, principal engineers, applied scientists, and product leaders to translate product vision into executable technical roadmaps, and you will represent the TPM function in leadership reviews .

This is not a coordination role. The right candidate will have deep technical judgment, understand distributed systems and ML inference pipelines, and bring the ability to make independent trade-off decisions in design reviews. You will own the mechanisms that keep these organizations operating at high velocity: pipeline health, deployment cadence, incident response posture, and cross-team dependency resolution. You will set the standard for how your TPMs operate, what they deliver, and how they develop.

Key job responsibilities
• Build, manage, and develop a team of Technical Program Managers across CRX and RAS program areas
• Drive cross-organizational programs that touch ad serving infrastructure, generative AI systems (LLM-based prompt pipelines, diffusion models, video assembly), multi-armed bandit selection frameworks, and demand-side platform integrations
• Establish and maintain mechanisms for operational excellence across both organizations
• Partner with engineering leadership (SDMs, PEs) to define technical roadmaps, identify architectural risks, and ensure that program milestones align with system capacity and dependencies
• Coach and develop TPMs at multiple levels, including direct mentorship of senior individual contributors preparing for principal-level promotion

A day in the life
You start your morning reviewing program metrics and narratives prepared by your team leads, identifying areas that need your attention or escalation. Mid-morning, you join a cross-functional review with engineering and product leaders to align on a critical initiative's milestones and resolve blockers. After lunch, you hold a one-on-one coaching session with one of your direct reports, discussing their team's delivery challenges and career development goals. Later, you facilitate a planning session where your team works backward from customer needs to define next quarter's priorities and resourcing strategy.

About the team
Creative Experience (CRX) CRX is responsible for the end-to-end lifecycle of ad creative on Amazon — from generation through optimization to final rendering at the point of impression. The organization consists of three core programs:
Advertiser Experience (AX) builds the tools and interfaces advertisers use to create, manage, and preview creatives within the Amazon DSP.
Universal Creative (UC) owns the asset lifecycle for all stages of assets, creatives, and the relationships of those to campaigns. It is the library for the creatives services.

RAS manages the integration layer between Amazon’s retail advertising products (Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, Sponsored Display) and the serving infrastructure that delivers ads across Amazon-owned and operated properties as well as third-party publisher inventory.

jobs.description:
AWS-Annapurna team develops the silicon used in our most advanced machine learning accelerator servers at cutting edge process nodes. These SoCs are used in massively scaled server clusters to provide best hardware platform for our customers to run training and inference workloads.

Our final product is a server, not just the silicon, so you will find yourself stretching beyond traditional silicon product engineering boundaries and dealing with various system issues and data sets, providing ample opportunities to learn.

We are looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to own end-to-end execution for complex silicon products from development through qualification, production ramp, and high-volume manufacturing.

You will own the integrated product schedule across Product Engineering, Test Engineering, Design, DFT, System Validation, Packaging, Quality, Reliability, Supply Chain, Foundry, OSAT, and external silicon partners.

This role requires you to be the owner of the outcome, not the status update -
You will identify the critical path, expose technical and execution risks early, establish clear owners and dates, drive decisions, and hold teams accountable for closure. You will dive deep enough into technical issues to identify owners, distinguish real blockers from noise and escalate when a decision is required.

Success means products hit committed milestones with the required quality, capacity, and manufacturing readiness

Key job responsibilities
Own the end-to-end silicon product schedule from tapeout and first silicon through bring-up, characterization, qualification, production release, ramp, and HVM.

Build and maintain integrated execution plans across silicon, package, test, quality, reliability, manufacturing, and supply-chain dependencies.

Define milestones, entry and exit criteria, owners, critical paths, and recovery plans.

Drive Product Engineering, Test Engineering, Design, DFT, Packaging, System Validation, Quality, Reliability, and Supply Chain teams to committed deliverables.

Dive deep on execution blockers; identify owner, root cause, decision required, and recovery path.

Drive closure of risks affecting schedule, quality, yield, test coverage, qualification, cost, capacity, or production readiness.

Own execution/communication of schedules and needs across foundry, OSAT and other external manufacturing partners.

Identify long-lead dependencies early, including wafer starts, masks, test hardware, package material, sockets, load boards, qualification hardware, equipment capacity, and translate product demand into manufacturing-capacity requirements and ensure capacity is available when the product needs it.

Drive readiness reviews for first silicon, characterization, qualification, production release, and volume ramp.

Establish mechanisms that expose schedule health, risks, decisions, and dependencies without relying on manual status collection.

Escalate early when teams cannot meet commitments. Bring options, trade-offs, and a recommended path.

Drive decisions when engineering quality, schedule, cost, capacity, and product requirements conflict.

Communicate program health to senior leadership with clear facts: what changed, why it matters, what decision is required, who owns the action, and when it will close.

Identify recurring execution failures and drive mechanism changes so the same problem does not reoccur on the next product.

Scale common planning, readiness, and execution mechanisms across multiple silicon programs.

About the team
Our team is focused on delivering technology programs that create real impact for Amazon's customers. We value collaboration, clear communication, and a willingness to tackle hard problems together. We are building an inclusive environment where program managers and engineers work side by side to simplify complex systems and ship meaningful improvements. If you are looking for a role where your program management expertise directly shapes outcomes and where you can grow alongside talented colleagues, this is the team for you.
Basic qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree in engineering, management, or technology
- 5+ years of experience in semiconductor product engineering, test engineering, silicon operations, manufacturing, or technical program management.
- Demonstrated ownership of semiconductor programs through major milestones such as tapeout, first silicon, bring-up, characterization, qualification, production release, ramp, or HVM.
- Working knowledge of semiconductor product-development and manufacturing flows across wafer fabrication, wafer sort, package assembly, final test, SLT, characterization, qualification, reliability, yield, and failure analysis.
- Experience driving execution across engineering teams that do not report to you.
Preferred qualifications:
- Experience with CPU, GPU, AI/ML accelerator, networking, or other large advanced-node SoCs.
- Experience driving products into high-volume manufacturing.
- Experience with advanced packaging, chiplets, 2.5D/3D integration, or HBM.
- Experience with ATE, SLT, product characterization, manufacturing test, yield ramp, and product qualification.
- Direct experience with leading foundry and OSAT partners.
- Experience managing capacity across wafer, package, assembly, and test.
- Experience owning multiple products or silicon generations concurrently.
- Experience creating execution mechanisms for a silicon organization that is scaling rapidly.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Leo Ground Systems Engineering
jobs.description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable broadband connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From households to small businesses, schools, hospitals, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve communities and organizations operating in places without dependable internet access.

The Ground Systems Engineering team is responsible for the ground segment infrastructure that connects Amazon Leo satellites to the terrestrial internet. As Amazon Leo scales into international markets, each piece of ground segment equipment must be certified and type-approved for operation in the destination country — a process known as homologation.

We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to own and drive the homologation program for GGT equipment across all target markets. You will be the central coordination point between engineering, regulatory, legal, trade compliance and third-party test laboratories, to ensure that all required certifications (EMC, safety, RF, environmental) are obtained on schedule. In addition to homologation, you will work with Software and Hardware Development teams, multiple suppliers, and other Leo Engineering teams to ensure internal and external requirements are met for the development and production of Gateway and TT&C terminals.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
In this role you will:
- Own the end-to-end homologation program for Ground System equipment across all target countries
- Manage relationships with third-party test laboratories (e.g., TÜV SÜD, UL, Intertek) and coordinate test scheduling, sample logistics, and report reviews
- Track and maintain a certification matrix mapping each equipment type to applicable standards (EMC, safety, RF, environmental, RoHS) by country
- Identify and escalate gaps in test coverage or standard edition mismatches, and work with engineering to resolve
- Maintain a living schedule of homologation milestones aligned to country launch timelines
- Provide TPM support to the newly formed Ground Technical Operations team
- Relentlessly simplify and demonstrate significant innovation, creativity, and good judgment when solving challenging problems
- Drive best practices on the team, deal with ambiguity and competing objectives, and proactively identify and mitigate risks before they become roadblocks
- Write effective narratives and present them concisely and effectively to senior management

About the team
The Ground Systems team is developing globally located high data rate satellite communication terminals which operate off of automated software driven systems and which maintain critical connectivity from the ground to the complete Leo constellation. This team is driving the development, deployment and long-term operability of Kuiper ground station terminals.
Basic qualifications:
- 3+ years of technical product or program management experience
- 3+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
- Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, or an equivalent engineering science
Preferred qualifications:
- 3+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
- Master's degree or above in a technical or engineering related field, such as Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, etc.
- Experience communicating technical concepts and processes using clear, simple language and visuals
- Knowledge of industry technologies in program or product domain (e.g., hardware, network, software, systems) and how to apply those technologies to solve problems
- Knowledge of project management tools

Every aspect of the Amazon global business depends on our systems to know who the customer is, and if our systems are not up and running, the company stops. jobs.title: Technical Program Manager - Field Integration and Testing , Amazon Leo
jobs.description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable broadband connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From households to small businesses, schools, hospitals, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve communities and organizations operating in places without dependable internet access.

Within the Experience Validation organization, the Field Integration and Testing (FIT) team pioneers end-to-end network field validation—testing Leo's full signal path from the customer terminal through gateway infrastructure to the internet, in real customer environments that labs cannot fully replicate. We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to drive the execution of FIT's core testing operations and its international expansion as Leo scales across territories and new hardware. You will be the connective tissue between FIT, Leo engineering, the Beta teams, and the Amazon Devices Field Quality Engineering (FQE) partnership, keeping test coverage aligned with a fast-moving release cadence of new customer terminals, firmware, and mobile app builds.

Key job responsibilities
In this role, you will own the program mechanics across FIT's three prioritized workstreams. For core operations, you will coordinate pre-release testing of new hardware and app releases before they reach Beta cohorts, create and drive resolution of bugs and quality issues, and track the health and uptime of the Solution Lab CT fleet as a shared resource for Leo teams. You will coordinate execution of country-specific functional test cases (e.g. regional IP routing, KPOP routing, Legal Interception) and B2B use cases—across Solution Labs in the Americas and EMEA, and support Solution Lab and demo center expansion into future markets. In the process ou will help operationalize the FQE partnership so expert testers can be dispatched to any country on short notice. Throughout, you will manage schedules, dependencies (including Beta Ops provisioning, hardware delivery, and spot enablement), open items, and risks, and maintain clear, data-backed status for leadership.

Success in this role requires strong technical program management judgment, comfort with networking and connectivity concepts, and the ability to coordinate many moving parts across teams, vendors, and geographies. You will define and report the metrics that show testing is on track and you anticipate dependencies and risks before they slip. You will write and communicate crisp and concise updates The ideal candidate is a hands-on, highly organized TPM who thrives in ambiguity, is comfortable working closely with engineers and field testers on production hardware and real integrations, and is energized by the challenge of proving out a brand-new satellite connectivity experience country by country.

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

You start your morning reviewing program dashboards and triaging any overnight issues that need immediate attention. By mid-morning you are leading a cross-team sync, aligning engineers and product partners on upcoming milestones and surfacing risks early. After lunch you might deep-dive into a technical design review, asking the right questions to ensure the proposed solution accounts for upstream and downstream impacts. Later, you draft a status narrative for leadership, distilling complex details into a clear story that drives decisions.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager III (TPM), Vendor EDI/API Integration — Mexico & Brazil, SCOT - Supplier Electronic Integration team
jobs.description:
Amazon’s Global Supplier Electronic integration team is seeking a Technical Program Manager (TPM III) to lead EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) and API (Application Programming Interface) integrations with Amazon’s external suppliers across Mexico and Brazil. The Supplier Electronic integration team powers the electronic integration flywheel behind the Amazon Retail Supply Chain, connecting suppliers to Amazon through automated data exchange.

In this role you will own several supplier integration projects in parallel and see each one through from first conversation to successful go-live. You will sit alongside the MX business teams and act as the bridge between two worlds: you translate business requirements and process needs into the right technical implementation, and you translate technical realities back into terms the business and the supplier understand. You will guide supplier SMEs and their IT teams through every aspect of our integration process, remove technical and process blockers, and drive excellence in data usage for the benefit of both the supplier and Amazon.

This is a role built for independence and collaboration at the same time. After an initial ramp-up period with our globally distributed team, you will be expected to be as self-sufficient as possible — making both the technical judgment calls and the strategic/tactical decisions needed to keep integrations moving. Beyond running projects, you will be on the pulse of the Mexico and Brazil business, building the strategy for how we make more vendor integrations happen: what makes it attractive for suppliers to integrate, which repetitive roadblocks to eliminate, and how EDI/API automation directly advances each country’s business goals when applied to a specific vendor’s situation.

Because this program is still early-stage in-region, you will get to pioneer with a business-development mindset — help the Mexico and Brazil business teams shaping the pitch to suppliers, codifying the recipe for a “perfect integration,” and continuously scaling the number of integrations that can be run in parallel. You will contribute to our documentation and AI-assisted tooling, feed ideas into our org’s improvement pipeline and feature roadmap, and be the voice of the MX/BR supplier back to our central product and tech teams.

The ideal candidate has a genuine technical background — enough to ramp up quickly on our systems, ask the right technical questions, judge trade-offs, and even build quick tooling for themselves — combined with the program-management discipline to run multiple projects cleanly, the business acumen to know why an integration matters to the country, and the communication skills to operate across languages and cultures. You are fluent in English and Spanish; Portuguese is a plus.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the lifecycle of a complex, cross-functional integration program spanning the Mexico and Brazil geographies. Manage multiple supplier EDI/API integrations in parallel — from concept and business-requirements gathering through technical implementation to successful go-live — with tactical execution and regional strategy ownership.

- Be the bridge between business and technology. Translate country and vendor business requirements into the right technical implementation, and translate technical realities back into business terms for suppliers and internal stakeholders. Deliver best-in-class, pro-active integration consultancy grounded in deep knowledge of our EDI/API solutions and the supplier's process and system blockers.

- Build and leverage strong relationships with external suppliers and 3rd party providers (including their SMEs, IT teams, and external service providers) and internal stakeholders to attract and grow adoption of our integration solutions.

- Own the region’s integration strategy. Stay on the pulse of the MX and BR business, understand how EDI/API automation advances each country’s goals, and build the strategy to drive more vendor integrations — making it more attractive for suppliers to integrate, evaluating and measuring the benefits for both Amazon and suppliers.

- Remove repetitive roadblocks and force-multiply. Identify recurring blockers across integrations, streamline or eliminate them, and codify the recipe for the “perfect integration and automation change management” so results scale beyond what one project-at-a-time allows.

- Operate with technical judgment and independence. After ramp-up, make sound technical and strategic/tactical decisions with limited guidance; understand our systems’ architecture, limitations, and the reasons behind design choices well enough to drive the right solution and mitigate the consequences of poor technology decisions.

- Contribute to documentation, AI solutions, and the product pipeline. Build and improve our integration documentation and AI-assisted tooling, and feed data-driven ideas from what you learn in-region into our org’s improvement pipeline and feature expansions.

- Be the voice of the MX/BR supplier. Add value with post-project analysis and case studies, influence our central product and tech teams on EDI/API tooling, and represent supplier needs internally.

- Deliver with rigor. Focus on goals with flexible prioritization and persistence; anticipate and overcome barriers; provide reliable reporting of your project activities, risks, mitigations, and outcomes; and make decisions that produce positive long-term impact.

- Communicate clearly to a wide range of audiences, from supplier IT teams to internal Directors — through status reports, narratives, and business/technical documentation.
Basic qualifications:
- 5+ years of technical program management working directly with software engineering teams experience
- 5+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
- Experience with APIs and technical integrations
- Experience in Business English skills, both verbal and written
- Engineering/technical background (e.g., CS/CE/EE degree or equivalent hands-on experience) sufficient to ramp up quickly, understand system architectures, APIs, and data flows, and drive constructive technical discussions with engineers.
- Experience working with external service providers as part of integration delivery.
- Experience managing multiple external-facing integration or delivery projects in parallel, including working with external suppliers, customers, or third-party service providers.
- Demonstrated ability to work directly with external partners/customers and their technical teams, and to translate between business requirements and technical implementation.
Preferred qualifications:
- Experience defining KPI's/SLA's used to drive multi-million dollar businesses and reporting to senior leadership
- Experience using AI-assisted development tools in academic or professional settings
- Professional proficiency in Portuguese.
- Experience in the Mexico and/or Brazil supplier landscape, or working across LatAm markets.
- Direct experience integrating external suppliers/vendors onto EDI/API platforms, ideally in a retail or supply-chain context.
- Business-development or program-scaling mindset — a track record of using data to define and achieve results, building pitch/marketing material, and growing adoption of a technical program.
- Data fluency: comfortable collecting and using data (SQL, logs, APIs, BI artifacts) to define and measure results and to drive data-driven decisions.
- Experience contributing to documentation, mechanisms, and product/feature improvements based on field learnings.

jobs.title: Sr. Technical Program Manager, Secure Space Builds, Cornerstone - Design, Build & Operations (DBO) Team
jobs.description:
Does working hard, making history and having fun resonate with your professional lifestyle? Do you like to be creative, solving challenges with innovative ideas? Do you feel passionate about designing and building secure facilities using structured project management methodologies?

The Cornerstone - Design, Build & Operations (DBO) Team owns and drives strategic, operational, and tactical initiatives to deliver secure spaces for AWS programs supporting our government customers globally. We empower organizations to achieve parity by offering flexible solutions that standardizes design and operations of secure spaces regardless of location, size, or customer.

This team is looking for an experienced project management professional to lead direct reports to meet strategic initiatives through cross functional teams to drive the planning, design and construction activities of secure office spaces to support the US Amazon Dedicated Cloud (ADC) communities.

This role requires someone with strong relationship building skills who will work with stakeholders on strategic planning/projects within Region Services organization. Some examples of project work may include support of delivering new or expanding current secure spaces.

You must be comfortable managing remote project delivery teams, and possess the ability to facilitate technical discussions to troubleshoot project management issues and remove barriers to project success.

The ideal candidate is exceptionally analytical and has a continuous improvement mindset. They have program management skill sets and a strong communicator (verbally and written) to collaborate to solve cross-organization challenges creatively.

If Arlington, VA (Arlington HQ2):

This role will sit in our new headquarters in Northern Virginia, where Amazon will invest $2.5 billion dollars, occupy 4 million square feet of energy efficient office space, and create at least 25,000 new full-time jobs. Our employees and the neighboring community will also benefit from the associated investments from the Commonwealth including infrastructure updates, public transportation improvements, and new access to Reagan National Airport.

By working together on behalf of our customers, we are building the future one innovative product, service, and idea at a time. Are you ready to embrace the challenge? Come build the future with us.

jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager, Amazon MGM Studios Financial Systems
jobs.description:
Ready to lead the successful integration of MGM's financial systems into Amazon?

Join Amazon MGM Studios Tech as the single-threaded owner of a multi-year program that migrates MGM's financial systems and the significant balance-sheet exposure and annual P&L activity they carry, out of multiple legacy platforms and into a single consolidated Amazon architecture. The Principal Technical Program Manager is a leadership role where you'll set strategic technical direction and drive a transformative, cross-organizational initiative spanning multiple business workstreams, a large portfolio of new deal types, across several engineering organizations, and a broad set of cross-functional stakeholders, with a firm deadline to fully deprecate MGM's legacy ERP and complete the integration.

What You'll Do:
- Own and deliver an ambiguous, very large, and complex program that spans multiple organizations and technology domains, serving as the single-threaded owner for all program-level milestones across several bespoke business workstreams (including international and domestic theatrical distribution, third-party content licensing, development and production, streaming, and production facilities).
- Design and own the end-to-end data migration and cutover strategy that moves all financial data (master, transactional, and reference data) from legacy systems to the consolidated platform, spanning the full stack across business, middleware, financial automation, downstream financial infrastructure, and legacy systems to deprecate.
- Develop workback plans per workstream, sequence migrations to manage operational risk, and coordinate with the studio's legal entity restructure, owning the sequencing trade-offs of its circular dependency with the program's builds.
- Own the standardization and graduation framework — define deal-type primitives, establish system-of-record boundaries, enforce standard-versus-exception rules, and determine when each workstream is ready to transition from the program to BAU ownership.
- Identify risks and opportunities in technical strategies, system architectures, and engineering organizational structures, resolving cross-workstream dependencies and engineering capacity gaps.
- Influence and advise VP-level leadership across multiple Finance Technology and Studios Technology organizations — plus Finance, Accounting, Tax, and FinOps — on technical investment decisions, organizational alignment, and long-term platform strategy, making priority calls based on business value, partner readiness, and platform reuse.
- Author the program's strategic narratives, define program-level tenets, and run the operating cadence (monthly and quarterly business reviews with senior leadership, and ad-hoc executive escalations).
- Drive clarity in a highly ambiguous environment where business strategy, architectural approach, and even the problem definition may not yet exist.

What You Bring:
- 10+ years of technical program management experience, with a demonstrated track record of delivering very large, cross-organizational programs.
- Deep expertise in large-scale systems and platform architecture, and the ability to evaluate and influence architectural strategies across multiple engineering organizations.
- Executive-level communication and influence skills, with experience advising VP-level leaders and aligning competing priorities across organizational boundaries — without direct line authority.
- Strong business acumen with the ability to connect technical decisions to business outcomes at scale.
- Experience making irreversible sequencing decisions in complex migrations and managing controllership and operational risk.

Why This Role Matters:
As the Principal TPM for this program, you won't just execute, you'll define how MGM's financial systems are successfully integrated into Amazon and rebuilt for the next decade. You'll make the irreversible calls: which businesses cut over first, when to freeze legacy systems, how to manage the circular dependency between the entity restructure and the program's builds, and which requirements to simplify without impacting customers. This is a role for someone who thrives in ambiguity, drives alignment across senior leaders with competing roadmaps, and delivers outsized, measurable business value and productivity impact.

This role reports to a Senior Manager of Software Development and regularly presents to VP-level leadership across the program's Steering Committee.

Join us in building the future of entertainment finance!

Prime Video (PV) Financial Systems (FinSys) calculates, pays, receives payments, accounts for and reports all financial activities to operate a digital streaming and studios business. We manage the onboarding of commercial contractual terms and enable seamless monetization of content and assets through mechanisms like PV related purchases, rentals, subscriptions, ads and theatrical releases. jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager, Customer Logistics Security (CLS)

Customer Logistics Security (CLS) within Stores Security (StoresSec) is seeking a Principal Technical Program Manager to define and deliver security programs with broad cross-organizational impact across Amazon's global logistics systems, from robotics platforms to the technology stacks that power worldwide fulfillment, transportation, and delivery operations.

Amazon's logistics network spans first mile (fulfillment and inbound), middle mile (sortation and transportation), and last mile (delivery) operations, along with Amazon Grocery and Amazon Prime Air drone-based delivery. Securing these systems at global scale requires identifying security gaps across diverse and rapidly evolving technology stacks, recognizing threat patterns that span operational boundaries, and driving a portfolio of security programs that protect customer trust and help ensure safe, reliable operations.

CLS builds and maintains security solutions that protect logistics and robotics infrastructure worldwide. This Principal TPM will operate with complete independence as the single-threaded leader responsible for identifying security risks across logistics systems and Amazon Robotics environments, defining technical requirements for CLS-built solutions, and influencing delivery of a portfolio of security projects across all logistics lines of business. You will be expected to operate in areas where security strategy has not yet been defined, applying deep knowledge of security systems and technologies to invent, evolve, improve, and simplify solutions. You will own the technology roadmap for CLS security solutions, decompose complex security problems into straightforward solutions, and drive large-scale engineering efforts that solve significantly complex or endemic security problems across Amazon's worldwide operations footprint.

This role requires deep security domain expertise and a broad understanding of the company systems and technologies relevant to logistics security. You will consistently bring strong, data-driven business and technical judgment to decisions, evaluate complex architectures spanning IT and operational technology boundaries, and influence senior stakeholders (VPs/SVPs) on security investment and prioritization. You will represent complex decisions, trade-offs, and potential solutions clearly to leaders up to three levels above, helping them understand the decisions they need to make and the options available.

- Security Risk & Threat Analysis: Assess logistics systems, robotics platforms, and operational technology across Amazon's worldwide operations, spanning first mile, middle mile, last mile, Grocery, and Prime Air, to identify security opportunities and systemic threat patterns. Identify gaps and opportunities within and between countries, architectures, and organizations. Recognize when systems are susceptible to prior failure patterns and steer teams to avoid recurrence.
- Technical Requirements, Design & Architecture Influence: Serve as a trusted representative of the CLS engineering organization, independently influencing system design and solution architecture across partner teams. Translate risk findings into clear technical requirements for CLS-built security solutions at global scale. Apply deep domain knowledge to invent new approaches where existing solutions fall short. Recognize when designs require additional guidance from senior engineers or subject matter experts and engage them appropriately.
- Portfolio Program Leadership: Own and drive a portfolio of security projects across all logistics lines of business. Make the case for technology programs, influence teams to dedicate resources, and lead the effort or find the appropriate owner. Ensure findings in one domain accelerate risk reduction in others.
- Strategy, Roadmaps & Delivery: Own the cross-functional program roadmap for Customer Logistics Security, operating in areas where strategy has not yet been defined. Drive large-scale engineering efforts end-to-end, from risk assessment through global deployment, creating the correct sense of urgency and aligning teams toward coherent security strategies.
- Stakeholder Influence & Communication: Build consensus and influence organization priorities, system owners, and technology direction across robotics engineering, logistics operations, and security organizations. Represent complex decisions and trade-offs clearly to leaders up to three levels above. Drive executive-level escalations with excellent judgment.
- Mentorship & Team Development: Amplify impact by educating TPM and engineering communities on security program management best practices. Mentor TPMs and program managers, participate in Principal TPM promotion assessments and talent reviews, and raise the bar on operational rigor and security domain expertise.

You will assess emerging risks as logistics systems and Amazon Robotics capabilities evolve, identify threat patterns that cut across operational boundaries, define what CLS needs to build next, and ensure delivery stays on track across a complex, multi-domain stakeholder landscape. We are looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to drive platform programs spanning 12+ tenants and 500+ developers as we evolve from a multi marketplace stack into a true multi business platform.

You will own the programs that turn a single business stack into versioned API contracts, a federated front end, and surface agnostic shopping capabilities that any Amazon business can configure into a journey of its own shape. Each tenant brings different needs, and your job is to sequence that work so businesses compose journeys instead of forking the platform.

This is a role for someone who thrives at the intersection of deep technical programs and many stakeholder coordination, who can hold a three year architectural direction while shipping quarter over quarter, and who cares that a page is ready in sub-second at Amazon volume.

Key job responsibilities
- Own cross team programs that deliver certified, versioned API contracts and a bring your own API extension path, so new businesses onboard by configuration rather than by forking the stack.
- Drive the front end federation program (shell, component registry, tenant packages, build time isolation) across feature teams shipping independently to production.
- Coordinate onboarding of new tenants and marketplaces, cutting time to launch from three months toward weeks, and track the platform effort each onboarding costs.
- Run the performance, resilience, and observability programs that keep every journey fast and tenant isolated at scale, including interaction budgets, alarm based rollback, and prevention of cross tenant incidents.
- Build the mechanisms that govern what earns a place in the shared core versus what stays a business owned extension, resolving competing tenant needs across 12+ clients.

You work with multiple senior and principal engineers on architecture tradeoffs, with product managers on which capabilities graduate into the core, and with partner teams on shared dependencies. You keep the performance and resilience bars visible, chase down a latency regression before it crosses tenants, and prep the quarterly checkpoint against annual targets. Your stakeholders span multiple leaders from fast growing businesses WW, and your customers are the Amazon teams building shopping experience using our platform.

About the team
We currently run the customer experience platform behind Amazon's quick commerce businesses. What began as one team's customer journey stack has grown into a single platform serving multiple marketplaces at roughly 700K orders a day. We are a B2B product whose customers are Amazon businesses, and our mission is to let any of them launch, experiment, and scale a shopping journey without building the stack beneath it. With millions of items moving in and out of an area twice as large as your average theme park every day, a quick peek under the roof would reveal a manic scene. jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager, Prime Video
jobs.description:
Prime Video (PV) is seeking a Principal Technical Program Manager (TPM) to own Operational Excellence and Development Efficiency across the business. Reporting directly to the Director of READI, this is a strategic, single-threaded leadership role for a builder who thrives in ambiguity and can set direction where the problem itself is not yet defined.

As a Principal TPM, you will operate across VP organizations, exercising broad strategic influence over how Prime Video plans, measures, and improves the operational health of its services and the productivity of its engineers. You will own high-visibility operating mechanisms — most notably the Prime Video Quarterly Operations Review — and set the overall strategy, goals, and initiatives for Operational Excellence across PV. You will manage significantly complex, cross-functional initiatives, remediate endemic problems, and force-multiply your impact through the mechanisms and standards you create. This is a role for someone who is regularly escalated to, rather than one who escalates.

Key job responsibilities
Operational Excellence Strategy & Goals

Define and own the multi-year strategy, annual goals, and initiative portfolio for Operational Excellence across Prime Video, aligning teams and organizations toward a simple, coherent approach.

Establish the operational metrics, standards, and paved-road practices that define what “good” looks like for PV services — covering availability, resilience, incident management, and operational readiness.

Set and track org-level operational goals planning, translating leadership priorities into measurable outcomes and holding teams accountable to them.

Remediate critical and endemic operational problems by identifying systemic root causes and driving durable, cross-org fixes rather than point solutions.

High-Visibility Mechanisms (PV Quarterly Operations Review)

Own the Prime Video Quarterly Operations Review end-to-end — its agenda, data, narrative, and follow-through — as the authoritative forum where PV leadership inspects operational health and commits to improvements.

Design, run, and continuously improve the portfolio of operating mechanisms (weekly/monthly business and ops reviews, metrics dashboards, and governance cadences) that create predictable inspection and drive action.

Curate crisp, accurate, and timely written narratives and data for senior leaders (up to and including VPs and S-Team-facing readouts), ensuring decisions are well-informed and action items are tracked to closure.

Create the connective tissue between mechanisms so that signals surfaced in one forum reliably drive prioritization, resourcing, and roadmap decisions across PV.

Development Efficiency

Own the strategy for improving developer productivity and delivery velocity across PV — reducing friction in the software lifecycle from design through deployment and operations.

Define and instrument developer efficiency metrics (e.g., build and deployment health, cycle time, change failure rate, time-to-recover) and use them to target the highest-leverage investments.

Drive adoption of paved-road tooling, standards, and best practices that simplify how PV teams build and operate, eliminating undifferentiated heavy lifting and unnecessary process.

Partner with builder-tools and infrastructure teams to unblock innovation and increase the speed and safety of delivery at scale.

Cross-Org Influence & Force Multiplication

Operate across VP organizations with broad strategic influence, building consensus, securing commitments, and negotiating positive outcomes among senior engineering and product leaders.

Drive clarity in ambiguity — frame problems that are not yet defined, align stakeholders on the path forward, and deliver with complete independence.

Force-multiply through the mechanisms, standards, and structures you create, raising the operational bar across teams without being in the critical path of every decision.

Actively develop the TPM community at PV — mentoring senior TPMs, contributing to promotion assessments, and elevating program-management craft across the organization.

A day in the life
No two days look the same, but the through-line is mechanism ownership and strategic influence. You might begin the morning diving deep into operational metrics ahead of the Quarterly Operations Review — pressure-testing the data, sharpening the narrative, and pre-aligning VP-org leaders on the decisions that need to be made. Midday, you facilitate a working session with engineering directors to unblock a cross-org resilience initiative, making the trade-off calls between business opportunity, resources, and long-term sustainability.

In the afternoon, you shift to development efficiency — reviewing delivery-velocity trends, identifying the systemic bottlenecks slowing teams down, and shaping the paved-road investments that will remove them. Throughout, you are the person leaders are escalated to when operational health is at risk, and the owner who ensures every commitment coming out of a mechanism is tracked to closure. Your success is measured not by the work you personally execute, but by the durable systems, standards, and mechanisms you leave behind.

About the team
READI is a central function in Prime Video that drives strategy, tooling, and programs for Scale Readiness, Operational Excellence, Resilience & Observability, and Development Efficiency. READI’s value as a central team relies heavily on outward-facing influence: its strategy, decisions, and guidance are amplified across all of PV. Prime Video operates a global, high-scale streaming service, spending hundreds of millions in infrastructure and allocating hundreds of engineers to operational load each year — a surface area where disciplined operational rigor and improved development efficiency translate directly into customer experience, cost, and speed of innovation.

Today, ownership of PV-wide Operational Excellence strategy and its supporting mechanisms is distributed, creating diffusion of responsibility and inconsistent standards across teams. This role exists to close that gap: to be the single-threaded owner who defines what operational excellence means for PV, instruments it, runs the mechanisms that inspect it, and drives the initiatives that continuously raise the bar.

- Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition

Most program roles ask you to coordinate other people’s work from a distance. FDE asks you to sit with the operational team and build the solution yourself. You take prototypes to production and hand scalable patterns back to the broader org.

Build AI & Agentic Solutions, Embedded

jobs.title: Sr TPM, Fwd Deployed Engineer , Business Innovation and AI
jobs.description:
The Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team within Business Innovation & AI (BIA) is looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager who builds. FDE embeds directly with teams across Amazon Global Operations Services (GOS), co-builds with them from day one, and ships working AI-powered solutions. Engagements range from short builds to multi-quarter programs. The impact here is internal: you build for the GOS org, not for external customers. We increasingly look for opportunities to replace manual processes and web-based interfaces with AI agents, so a lot of what you build will be agentic.

This is an FDE role first, with a data engineering edge. The core of the job is building AI and agentic solutions embedded with operational teams. On top of that, you own the team’s data and data-engineering strategy and infrastructure, the pipelines and architecture and data-quality decisions our AI work depends on.

This is a builder role. We’re looking for people who are already shipping AI solutions with the current generation of tooling, not people who are newly exploring AI or have only done some prompt engineering. The engineers who do well here are hands-on with agentic harnesses like Claude Code, Kiro, and Codex, and are plugged into the AI builder community closely enough to know what changed this month.

Key job responsibilities
Build AI & Agentic Solutions, Embedded (the primary work)
- Embed with GOS operational teams, co-build from day one, and ship AI-powered solutions that change how work gets done
- Look for opportunities to replace manual processes and web-based interfaces with AI agents, and build those agents end to end
- Build with the current AI tooling yourself, including agentic harnesses (Claude Code, Kiro, Codex), LLM application frameworks, and RAG, and take prototypes to production

Program Delivery
- Drive the planning, coordination, and delivery of FDE’s AI programs, managing risk and dependencies without relying on direct authority
- Turn ambiguous operational problems into shipped solutions, and own the longer-horizon programs where the answer takes more than one build cycle

Data & Data-Engineering Strategy (the DE edge)
- Own the team’s data and data-engineering strategy and infrastructure: the architecture, technology choices, and roadmap our AI work depends on
- Make the calls on how operational data becomes AI-ready, and keep data quality, lineage, and freshness where the team can trust it
- Connect source data to what the customer actually needs: find the right source, get the subscription in place, and build the pipeline that keeps it flowing
- Make and defend the opinionated architecture calls (lakehouse vs. warehouse, batch vs. streaming, how far to normalize a domain), grounded in each use case

Raising the Bar
- Define the reusable patterns and standards that raise the bar for the whole team, and mentor engineers on them

A day in the life
You start the morning embedded with an operations team, working through a manual workflow you’re replacing with an agent. By mid-morning you’re building against it with current tooling and putting the next iteration in front of them. In the afternoon you switch to the data side, making the call on how a new data domain gets modeled and subscribed into the platform so the agent has what it needs. You close the day reviewing a teammate’s design against the patterns you set, and re-cutting the roadmap for a program that has two quarters left to run.

About the team
Business Innovation & AI (BIA) finds the hardest, highest-value problems across Amazon Global Operations Services and builds AI-powered solutions that measurably change how work gets done. Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) is BIA’s technical execution arm: a small, senior team with high autonomy and a bias for shipping. We embed with operational teams in the GOS org, co-build from day one, ship working solutions, and hand scalable patterns off to the broader organization. We don’t just automate the existing process; we redesign the work around what AI and agents make possible.

- Experience developing, deploying and managing AI products at scale
- Knowledge of data engineering pipelines, cloud solutions, ETL management, databases, visualizations and analytical platforms
- Experience with SQL and Python scripting
- Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, mathematics or equivalent, or Bachelor's degree or above in computer science, engineering, analytics, mathematics, statistics, IT or equivalent
- Experience with AWS data services (S3, Glue, Athena, Redshift, or an equivalent cloud data stack)
- Experience driving technical programs across multiple teams without direct authority

jobs.description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Within Data Center Engineering, the Security Solutions team is the newest generations of Security technologies from concept to production readiness in our data centers. Our engineers solve challenging technology problems and take big bets on new concepts enabling AWS services to continue to revolutionize the industry. This role provides the opportunity to engage with and lead the Technical Program Management aspect for these advanced cloud infrastructure solutions and the exceptional people that develop them. During a new device deployment, the Sr. Technical Program Manager understands the end customer’s needs to ensure successful product deployment from production to launch, to make Data Center operations more efficient, safe, and secure.

Key job responsibilities
• Build strategic plans for new Security Solutions and methods to reach maturity for global deployment.
• Plan for global and regional nuances, test and validate, create deployment schedules, and similar production readiness actions
• Lead the development, deployment, and sustainment of Security Systems for our next generation data center in a highly cross-functional environment, which includes internal customers, hardware, and software development teams.
• Provide program management leadership in the application of new technologies and/or retro-fit type work to enable large scale hardware deployments in a continuous effort to deliver a world-class customer experience.
• Drive teams across multiple organizations to deliver complex cross-functional programs with high impact to the organization.

A day in the life
Our TPMs work closely with key partners to innovate, create, manage, and deliver holistic programs, and ensure products are fully production ready at launch. “Production ready at launch” addresses requirements for a product to be viable for global deployment: approved financials, technical specifications and designs, supplier sourcing and qualification, testing, operations training, and similar requirements. We build and execute the plan that addresses requirements in these areas, resulting in a product or solution that is production ready for global deployment.

About the team
The Security Solutions team provides engineering expertise and design support for security products in data centers globally. We own and support security products throughout their lifecycle. Our scope also includes emergent global scale remediation strategic efforts that impact Data Center capacity or availability and introducing and driving business improvement initiatives increasing visibility and enabling data driven decision making. The team ranges from hardware development to software / system development across the US, Europe and Asia Pacific.

Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Hybrid Work
We value innovation and recognize this sometimes requires uninterrupted time to focus on a build. We also value in-person collaboration and time spent face-to-face. Our team affords employees options to work in the office every day or in a flexible, hybrid work model near one of our US Amazon offices.

jobs.title: Sr Technical Program Manager, Proactive Security (Level 6)
jobs.description:
Cryptographically relevant quantum computers could break the classical cryptography that protects the confidentiality and integrity of Amazon customers' data. As the industry accelerates its post-quantum cryptography (PQC) readiness timelines, Specialized Business Security (SBS) must reason about and migrate an unusually diverse portfolio: devices already in customers' homes, future devices, protected content on third-party devices, and customer traffic across satellite and ground infrastructure. As Technical Program Manager for the SBS-wide PQProgram, you will own the cross-cutting PQC problems shared across teams and turn a fast-evolving, ambiguous space into clear tracked plans, and measurable readiness outcomes.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the end-to-end PQC journey for shared crypto problems: code signing, PKI infrastructure, Crypto Bill of Materials (CBOM), and PQC migration of backend services.
- Coordinate PQC work across Amazon organizations, importing and exporting reusable techniques and artifacts so related hardware and software efforts build on each other rather than in isolation.
- Enumerate PQC readiness across device-relevant industry standards (Matter, Bluetooth, OAuth 2.0, DRM), clarify each standard's trajectory, and drive informed next steps with product and security teams.
- Define program strategy, objectives, and success metrics; align stakeholders; and drive delivery across engineering teams while navigating crypto trade-offs, including device form-factor constraints (limited RAM/ROM/CPU).
- Run recurring program business reviews, proactively identify and mitigate risk, and write and present narratives to senior leadership.

A day in the life
You review PQProgram metrics, then facilitate a design discussion on PQC migration for a constrained device, weighing algorithm options against RAM/ROM/CPU limits. You join a cross-organization working session to reuse a PQC approach already solved elsewhere in Amazon, draft a section of an upcoming leadership review, and update the standards tracker. Some days you drive execution on a well-defined problem; others you convert genuine ambiguity into a plan the org can follow.

About the team
SBS Core secures a diverse set of Amazon businesses, working backwards from what products need to be secure. The SBS-wide PQProgram coordinates and executes the post-quantum cryptography work shared across these businesses. We value clear thinking, learning quickly in an evolving field, and taking ownership of hard, ambiguous problems that grow more important as the quantum timeline accelerates.

jobs.title: Senior HW TPM, Amazon Robotics OBDA-Sortation
jobs.description:
Amazon Robotics is seeking a talented and motivated Senior Technical Program Manager to lead hardware program delivery for the Sortation Vertical. You will own the full program lifecycle for next-generation sortation hardware — from concept through engineering validation, multi-site deployment, and sustaining support in the field.

Are you inspired by invention? Is problem solving through teamwork in your DNA? Do you like the
idea of seeing how your work impacts the bigger picture? Answer yes to any of these and you'll fit
right in here at Amazon Robotics. We are a smart team of doers that work passionately to apply
advances in robotics and software to solve real-world challenges that will transform our customers'
experiences in ways we can't even imagine yet.

This role sits on the Sortation Hardware Engineering team and is the single-threaded program owner for our hardware portfolio. You will drive the mechanical and electromechanical programs that deploy into Amazon's Sortation Centers at scale, working across Systems Engineering, Deployment Engineering, Solutions, Manufacturing and Supply Chain, Product, and Customer Support. You will own the program schedule, the change-control cadence, the supplier and procurement path, and the launch readiness gate — and you will be accountable when those slip.

You will be successful in this role if you are equally comfortable running a design review, chasing
a long-lead component through a contract manufacturer, and standing on a sort center floor at 6am during an install.

Key job responsibilities
• You will own end-to-end delivery of sortation hardware programs across all engineering disciplines, holding the schedule and the critical path across teams that do not report to you and driving technical decisions to closure on the record.
• You will own the change-control cadence for the hardware portfolio, ensuring our contract manufacturers and deployment partners build to the released revision.
• You will own the procurement path for program hardware, translating supplier lead times on long-lead components into schedule risk before they become launch impacts.
• You will own launch readiness for site deployments through the go/no-go decision and the handover to site Reliability Maintenance Engineering and Operations, and you will sustain solutions already in the field.

A day in the life
One morning you are deciding whether a bracket that does not fit stops a live install. That afternoon you are working out whether a cable assembly running three weeks late moves a launch date, and pushing a stalled engineering change through to release. Some weeks you are at your desk owning the schedule and the readiness summary leadership will read before a site goes live. Some weeks you are on a sort center floor with a tape measure. Both are the job.
Basic qualifications:
- 5+ years of technical program management experience
- Experience managing programs across cross-functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Manufacturing, or Industrial Engineering, or a related technical field
- 5+ years of experience working directly with hardware engineering teams
- Experience taking electromechanical hardware from prototype through production and field deployment
Preferred qualifications:
- 7+ years of technical program management experience
- Experience designing or implementing integrated automation solutions such as material handling systems, high-speed packaging lines, or manufacturing lines
- 4+ years of change management experience
- Experience managing contract manufacturers and long-lead component supply chains, including translating lead-time risk into schedule impact
- Experience managing NPI validation gates (EVT/DVT/PVT) and multi-site deployment launches
- Experience with capital planning and procurement mechanics — purchase requisitions, capital requests, and vendor qualification
- Experience owning technology handover to a maintenance or operations organization
- Master's degree, MBA, or PMP certification
