jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager (SW/FW) , AWS Hardware Engineering
jobs.description:
Every server in an AWS data center runs firmware, and someone has to decide how a new version of it safely reaches millions of machines. That is this role: you will own how firmware ships across the AWS server fleet, and you will design the mechanisms that make it predictable and safe at that scale.

We build the software that lives closest to the hardware, including BMC, BIOS, and the controllers that manage power, cooling, sensors, and health on every server and rack we deploy. Writing that firmware is only half the problem. Getting a new version onto millions of machines, in the right order, at the right time, without disrupting a single customer, is the other half. That half is yours.

Your real product is the mechanisms. You will design the repeatable machinery that gets every release to the finish line without heroics: a release calendar the whole organization plans against, quality gates with clear criteria a build must clear before it goes anywhere near production, a staged rollout model that limits exposure if something goes wrong, and one shared view of where every release stands so nobody has to ask. You will define how teams hand off to each other, how a blocker gets escalated and by when, and how we know a rollout is actually healthy rather than just finished.

Every server in an AWS data center runs firmware, and someone has to decide how a new version of it safely reaches millions of machines. That is this role: you will own how firmware ships across the AWS server fleet, and you will design the mechanisms that make it predictable and safe at that scale.

We are looking for an experienced Senior Technical Program Manager to own firmware release and deployment across our firmware teams. You will work across firmware engineering, hardware engineering, manufacturing partners, service teams, and security to make firmware delivery predictable, repeatable, and safe at fleet scale.

We build the software that lives closest to the hardware, including BMC, BIOS, and the controllers that manage power, cooling, sensors, and health on every server and rack we deploy. Writing that firmware is only half the problem. Getting a new version onto millions of machines, in the right order, at the right time, without disrupting a single customer, is the other half. That half is yours.

Your real product is the mechanisms. You will design the repeatable machinery that gets every release to the finish line without heroics: a release calendar the whole organization plans against, quality gates with clear criteria a build must clear before it goes anywhere near production, a staged rollout model that limits exposure if something goes wrong, and one shared view of where every release stands so nobody has to ask. You will define how teams hand off to each other, how a blocker gets escalated and by when, and how we know a rollout is actually healthy rather than just finished.

You will get to decide what good looks like here, then make it stick. That means finding the places where coordination happens by memory or by meeting and replacing them with something documented, measured, and ideally automated. It means using every release and every operational surprise as evidence, turning what you learn into a permanent change to the process or the tooling instead of a one-time fix. And it means holding a high bar with engineering teams who do not report to you, which you will earn through being right and being useful rather than through org chart authority.

What makes this different from most program management jobs:

- You will work where software meets physical hardware. A bad firmware rollout does not just throw an error, it can take a machine offline, so the bar for getting it right is unusually high.
- Your scope is the whole fleet. Decisions you make about release process apply to millions of servers across every AWS region.
- You are building the mechanisms, not inheriting them. There is real room to design how this works rather than administer someone else's process.
- You will get deep in the technology. This is a hands-on technical role with engineers, not a status-reporting role.

If you like turning messy, high-stakes coordination into something that runs predictably, and you want to see your work land at a scale very few places can offer, we would like to talk to you. AWS engineers are shaping the way people use computers and designing the future of cloud computing technology, come help us make history!

Key job responsibilities
Own firmware release and deployment end to end, from a completed code change through qualification to a fully deployed fleet.
Publish and maintain the release schedule that the firmware teams plan against, and drive agreement on scope, sequencing, and dependencies between them.
Define the quality gates a release must pass at each stage, including hardware qualification and validation at our manufacturing partners, and hold teams to the entry and exit criteria.
Build and run the reporting that shows where every release stands, how much of the fleet is on the current version, and what is blocking progress, and present that to senior leadership on a regular cadence.
Own escalation for release blockers, including issues raised by manufacturing partners, and drive them to closure against a defined response time.
Turn what we learn from each release and each operational issue into a lasting change to the process, the gates, or the tooling.
Partner with firmware, hardware, manufacturing, security, and service teams to resolve competing priorities and keep releases moving.
Find the coordination that happens manually today and replace it with automation.

A day in the life
You will spend time with the firmware engineering teams, going deep on what is in the next release, what changed, what worries them, and whether it is ready to move to the next stage. These are technical conversations, not status checks, and you will be expected to hold your own in them.
You will spend time on releases already in flight. That means looking at how a staged rollout is progressing, deciding whether the data supports widening it, and pulling the handle to pause or roll back when it does not. When something fails qualification or a manufacturing partner reports a problem, you are the person who gets the right people on it and keeps it moving until it is closed.
You will spend time building. Writing down a gate that only existed in people's heads, replacing a manual status roll-up with something automated, tightening a handoff between two teams that keeps slipping, updating the release schedule as reality changes.
And you will spend time communicating. Giving leadership a clear read on where releases stand and what the risks are, aligning teams whose priorities are in tension, and making the case for a decision that not everyone will initially agree with.

About the team
The AWS Hardware Engineering team designs the servers behind AWS, from general purpose compute and storage to the GPU and AI accelerator systems used for machine learning and generative AI. These systems run at high power and thermal density and are deployed in large clusters, where the health of a single server can affect a whole training job. Our firmware manages that hardware: power, cooling, sensors, health reporting, and its own updates. In this role you would own how that firmware reaches servers across the fleet.

- 5+ years of technical product or program management experience
- 7+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
- 3+ years of software development experience
- 5+ years of technical program management working directly with software engineering teams experience
- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
- 3+ years of experience delivering technical programs in a firmware, embedded systems, or hardware development environment
Preferred qualifications:

- Experience managing projects across cross functional teams, building sustainable processes and coordinating release schedules
- Experience defining KPI's/SLA's used to drive multi-million dollar businesses and reporting to senior leadership
- Experience owning firmware, embedded software, BIOS, or operating system release and deployment programs at fleet scale Experience with server hardware or data center infrastructure, including hardware qualification and validation with manufacturing partners Experience with CI/CD pipelines, staged rollout and canary strategies, and change safety mechanisms for software or firmware deployments

jobs.title: Sr. Technical Program Manager, Trust CX Innovations
jobs.description:
Trust depends on two things being true at once: that every piece of customer data is governed, controlled, and provably compliant, and that the organization can move fast enough to keep up as products evolve in the era of AI. TCI's AI Enablement & Data Governance charter owns both. On the data side, we make sure data is classified, its handling is enforceable, and compliance can be proven rather than asserted. On the enablement side, we use AI-driven automation to take operational load off the entire organization so builders spend their time building trust, not maintaining it by hand.

We are looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to drive the programs across this charter. You will own complex, cross-functional initiatives that span product, engineering, and science teams, and often multiple organizations, from data governance and enforcement programs to the automation efforts that reduce operational burden at scale. Operating with significant autonomy, you will set the plan, map dependencies across teams, surface risks early, and keep a broad set of stakeholders aligned on a shared bar and timeline, including partners in privacy, legal, and other organizations we depend on. You will operate at a technical level, understanding the systems and trade-offs well enough to ask the right questions and drive sound decisions, and you will bring the judgment and influence to hold teams that do not report to you accountable to their commitments. Above all, you will be the connective tissue that turns provable data governance and AI-driven efficiency from goals into delivered outcomes.

Key job responsibilities
- Own and drive complex, cross-functional programs across both data governance and AI enablement, spanning multiple engineering, product, and science teams and often multiple organizations.
- Build the program plan from ambiguity: define scope, milestones, and success criteria, and translate a broad charter into an executable roadmap with clear owners.
- Map and manage cross-team and cross-org dependencies, including partners in privacy and legal, surface risks early, and drive them to resolution before they affect delivery.
- Drive data governance programs so that data classification, handling enforcement, and retention obligations are met and provable, and make those requirements a prerequisite for new services rather than an afterthought.
- Drive the AI enablement and automation agenda that reduces operational burden across the organization, and track its impact on capacity and delivery.
- Establish the bar for what "done" and "compliant" mean in this space and embed it into how programs are planned and run.
- Keep a diverse set of stakeholders aligned, from individual builders to senior leaders, through clear written narratives, status, and decision documents.
- Operate at a technical level: understand the systems and trade-offs well enough to ask the right questions, challenge assumptions, and drive sound decisions.

jobs.description:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) Hardware Engineering is a fast growing and leading-edge research and development team that creates enterprise compute and storage server designs for our innovative web service and e-commerce technology platforms. Our designs are industry-leading in terms of performance, frugality and operational excellence, and are critical to the success of the AWS business and the hundreds of thousands of customers who use utility computing today.

We are seeking an experienced Technical Program Manager (TPM) to define and build the next generation of our cloud servers. Our success depends on our highly respected server infrastructure; we’re handling massive scale and rapid integration of emergent technologies.

The ideal TPM candidate will be an experienced program manager who is skilled in managing hardware product development teams across several geographic regions using a variety of suppliers. The successful candidate will be an innovative self-starter and leader. The candidate will be familiar with the cloud computing industry and AWS offerings and will be passionate about providing the best possible customer experience at the best cost. The candidate will have an obsession with data and precise analysis and will use these as inputs to make decisions.

Key job responsibilities
•You manage large, complex technology initiatives, delivering critical solutions, significant improvements, new mechanisms, or deprecating systems that are no longer needed.
•You successfully manage all stages (from concept to delivery).
•You work closely with your customers to understand their short and long term business goals and product needs.
•You are responsible for the delivery of platforms through driving and coordinating the efforts of an interdisciplinary team across hardware design, component development, firmware, test, and qualification, along with external suppliers and design partners to develop, deploy at scale, and provide ongoing operational support for the servers you deliver.
•You are actively involved in the sustaining operational health of the platforms you support
•You understand the architecture of the systems you work with (e.g., workflows, APIs, runtime characteristics, design limitations, and maintenance requirements). You influence team technical priorities and business strategy through data-driven contributions.
•You communicate ideas effectively, verbally and in writing, to a wide range of audiences including Directors and VPs. You foster a constructive dialogue, harmonize discordant views, and lead the resolution of contentious issues (build consensus). You partner successfully with customers, stakeholders, and engineering teams.
•Your program management practices set a great example to others. You routinely and efficiently deliver the right things. You define clear goals and objectives. You drive crisp decisions in your program area about what projects move forward and in what priority order. You proactively identify risks and bring them to the attention of your team and stakeholders with plans for mitigation before they become roadblocks.
•You are a simplifier. You judiciously add, refine, and remove procedures. By applying project management best practices, you increase the productivity and effectiveness of the teams you work with.

A day in the life
What you will do: As a TPM on the Specialized Platforms and Servers Hardware Engineering team you will be responsible for leading AWS EC2 Enterprise fleet operations and hardware product development programs in a highly cross-functional environment which includes internal customers, external vendors and technology partners. You’ll provide leadership in the application of new technologies to large scale server deployments in a continuous effort to deliver a world-class customer experience at a world-class cost point. This is a fast-paced challenging position, and you’ll work with thought leaders in multiple technology areas. You’ll have high standards for yourself and everyone you work with, and you’ll be constantly looking for ways to improve your product’s performance, quality and cost. Using data and key metrics, you will also drive and measure process improvements that enhance our operational effectiveness. You will work in a dynamic, challenging, and fast-changing organization. We’re changing an industry, and we need leaders who are ready for this challenge and who want to reach beyond what is possible today.

Why you will love it: You will have exposure to teams and leaders across the entire company. You will be a part of a leading edge research and development team. You will see many aspects of the Amazon business. You will have a direct impact on our bottom line and the ability to improve things for our developers. You will be part of a growing, fast paced, and fun team. You will have ownership and responsibility for defining and executing processes that deliver both savings and productivity for Amazon.

About the team
You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. You’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Utility Computing (UC)
AWS Utility Computing (UC) provides product innovations — from foundational services such as Amazon’s Simple Storage Service (S3) and Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2), to consistently released new product innovations that continue to set AWS’s services and features apart in the industry. As a member of the UC organization, you’ll support the development and management of Compute, Database, Storage, Internet of Things (IoT), Platform, and Productivity Apps services in AWS, including support for customers who require specialized security solutions for their cloud services.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Run a single view of capability adoption: Maintain source of truth for the full portfolio of tracked capabilities across the three businesses, with dependency maps and effort sizing, and represent it in global planning and review forums.

Sequence cross-team dependencies: Untangle the multi-team dependency chains that cause launches to slip, coordinating across engineering, product, finance/compliance, and operations teams.

Alongside the day-to-day, you're steering the India launch of a multi-million-dollar product — coordinating engineering, finance, and operations across two continents to bring a capability to one of Amazon's most important growth markets.

jobs.description:
Amazon Web Services Open Data Analytics (ODA) organization is looking for a Technical Program Manager to drive cross-team programs spanning release infrastructure, query engine development, and datalake integrations across Amazon EMR, AWS Glue, and Amazon Athena.

ODA powers millions of clusters across all AWS regions, enabling customers to run massive-scale analytics using open-source frameworks like Apache Spark, Trino, Apache Iceberg, Hudi, and Delta. Our teams build the automated release pipelines that package and distribute production-ready releases across multiple deployment modes (EC2, EKS, Serverless), and develop the core query engine optimizations that deliver 5x+ performance improvements over open-source baselines.

We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to coordinate complex, cross-cutting programs across our Release Automation (Fundamentals) and Engines teams. You will drive end-to-end delivery of programs that span release pipeline modernization, engine performance initiatives, open-source upstream integrations, and region expansion. You will manage dependencies across teams, identify and mitigate risks, and ensure that our engineering investments translate into measurable customer outcomes.

Key job responsibilities
Own and drive cross-team program execution for release automation, engine performance, and datalake integration initiatives spanning Amazon EMR, AWS Glue, and Amazon Athena.
Build and maintain integrated program schedules across the Fundamentals and Engines teams, tracking milestones, dependencies, and critical path items across release pipeline modernization, region expansion, and engine optimization workstreams.
Identify, assess, and mitigate risks that span team boundaries — escalating early when release pipeline issues threaten downstream engine delivery or when upstream open-source changes impact release timelines.
Define program metrics and mechanisms (WBRs, dashboards, program reviews) to measure release velocity, pipeline reliability, engine performance benchmarks, and operational toil reduction.
Drive region build programs end-to-end, coordinating infrastructure readiness, release validation, and service launch activities across multiple AWS regions and deployment modes (EC2, EKS, Serverless).

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Availability Serviceability Team
jobs.description:
The AWS Data Center Availability Serviceability team works with hundreds of AWS data centers globally to deliver the highest quality and lowest cost availability, capacity, and scaling results for our customers. We standardize operations globally by delivering tools, policy, processes, and procedures to our internal teams.

Serviceability is the ability to maintain, repair, and manage infrastructure assets efficiently throughout their lifecycle -- encompassing maintenance standards, spares management, training and certifications, operational readiness, and the systematic use of data and automation to prevent disruptions and drive continuous improvement.

We are seeking a Technical Program Manager to own the MBOM program as part of the AWS Data Center Availability Serviceability Critical Spares team. MBOMs define which parts make up each piece of critical infrastructure equipment and are foundational to programmatic spares planning and fulfillment -- enabling proactive stocking decisions, criticality assessments, and repair readiness across the global fleet.

What you will do:

You will own the development and delivery of a multi-year roadmap to establish comprehensive MBOM coverage across the global AWS fleet. Working with stakeholders across Field Engineering, DCEO, vendors, and lifecycle data teams, you will scale AI-powered pipelines that extract MBOM data from vendor documentation, define per-equipment MBOM standards, and design the processes for establishing MBOMs where source documentation does not exist. Your work sets the foundation for programmatic spares identification, criticality assessment, and fulfillment -- ensuring the right parts are available at the right locations before failures occur. You will build the mechanisms that keep MBOM data current as the fleet grows, diversifies into new cooling technologies, and introduces new vendors.

Why it matters:

Spares readiness starts with knowing what's inside the equipment. MBOM is the data layer that connects equipment design to spares strategy to repair outcomes. With comprehensive MBOM coverage, we can programmatically identify critical parts, make proactive stocking decisions, and reduce time to repair -- directly improving data center availability for customers.

Why you will love it:

You will own a program that is genuinely novel -- building something that didn't exist two years ago, using AI tooling that is still maturing, against a problem (fleet-wide MBOM completeness) that no one has solved at this scale. You will operate in high ambiguity with real ownership to define what good looks like. You will work across PLM systems, enterprise asset management, spares strategy, and physical equipment -- giving you breadth that most TPM roles don't offer. And your output has direct, measurable impact: every MBOM you complete makes the fleet more repairable.

Key job responsibilities
- Own MBOM program strategy, execution, and completeness metrics across the global fleet
- Operate and scale AI-assisted pipelines that convert vendor documentation into governed MBOM records
- Define and execute the process for establishing MBOMs where vendor documentation is limited or unavailable
- Ensure MBOM data flows into criticality assessments and stocking decisions within the Critical Spares program
- Define per-equipment MBOM standards in partnership with Field Engineering and equipment owners
- Build mechanisms to maintain MBOM accuracy as new equipment deploys and the fleet evolves (including liquid cooling)
- Drive cross-functional coordination across Availability, Field Engineering, DCEO, and lifecycle data teams
- Use data and metrics to measure program health, prioritize effort, and communicate progress
- Write narratives (one to six pages) and present to Director-level leadership
- Travel up to 10%

A day in the life
You will split your time between program execution and cross-functional coordination. On any given day you might be reviewing AI pipeline output quality with the tooling team, defining MBOM standards for a new equipment type with Field Engineering, working with a vendor to obtain documentation for legacy equipment, analyzing coverage gaps to prioritize the next tranche of MBOMs, or presenting program status and trade-off decisions to leadership. You will operate at both the strategic level - setting the roadmap for fleet-wide MBOM completeness - and the tactical level - digging into specific equipment families where data doesn't exist.
Basic qualifications:
- 3+ years of technical product or program management experience
- 3+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
- 2+ years of analytical, quantitative, communication, and presentations experience
- 2+ years of experience with bill of materials, spare parts management, or enterprise asset management (CMMS/PLM) systems
Preferred qualifications:
- Experience with data analysis tools such as Excel, Pivot Tables, SQL, Tableau, etc.
- Knowledge of data center infrastructure design, operations, or delivery
- Experience working closely with development and business teams to communicate problem impacts and to understand business requirements
- Experience interpreting technical or engineering documentation such as drawings, parts lists, vendor manuals, or specifications
- Experience operating or managing AI/ML-assisted tools, automation pipelines, or data engineering workflows
- Experience working with vendor technical teams or OEM partners

jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager, AppSTAR COMPASS
jobs.description:
Own the program that brings security review into the LLM age, on a brand-new team building it at Amazon scale. You'll drive an effort that touches tens of thousands of engineers, a dozen partner teams, and a security review model the company is rebuilding from the ground up.

Security review has always been a bottleneck. A developer ships a change, waits for someone to look at it, and the security team drowns in a queue it can never fully clear. We're ending that tradeoff. Our engine evaluates changes as they happen, decides how much scrutiny each one actually needs, and handles the common case automatically: no wait for the developer, no queue for the reviewer.

The hard part isn't any single system. It's the seams! The signal sources we depend on, the platforms we write into, the reviewers whose workflow we're changing, and the teams whose roadmaps have to line up with ours. That's the job. The team is funded and forming now, and you'll be the person who turns a strategy into a sequenced plan with owners, dates, and evidence that it worked.

- Own a technically deep program end to end, from requirements through a measured pilot to scaled rollout
- Work across engineering, security, and platform teams with real dependencies and real deadlines
- Define what success looks like and hold the program to it

Key job responsibilities
- Own the program end to end: requirements, plan, sequencing, dependencies, risks, and delivery against measurable goals.
- Run the requirements pass across every group in the loop, including the engineers whose changes get evaluated, the security engineers who handle escalations, and the managers who staff and measure the work, and turn what you learn into a concrete build backlog.
- Manage the cross-team dependencies this platform runs on: the telemetry and signal sources feeding it, the visibility platforms it writes into, and the classification data it consumes. Negotiate interfaces and get them onto partner roadmaps.
- Design and run a bounded pilot with explicit exit criteria, then drive the decision about what happens next based on what the data says.
- Define the metrics that tell us the system is working: how accurately it routes, how well its confidence tracks reality, and whether escalations reach resolution.
- Drive crisp technical decisions in design reviews. Ask the questions that surface risk early, and escalate with judgment when a dependency slips.
- Own program communication to senior leadership: status, tradeoffs, and risk, stated plainly.
- Build the operating rhythm for a new team from scratch, and keep process to the minimum that actually helps.

A day in the life
You'll start most days on dependencies: which partner team owes you an interface, what slipped, what you need to escalate. Midday you're in a design review asking whether a decision creates a problem two quarters out, or interviewing reviewers to understand how they actually work before we build for them. Afternoons you're in the data, checking whether the pilot is hitting its exit criteria and writing the update that goes to leadership. Some weeks you're building the plan; others you're rebuilding it because the pilot told you something inconvenient.

About the team
We're a new team with a specific job: decide how security attention gets spent, and make that decision automatically. Our customers are the engineers shipping code and the security engineers reviewing it. Today both pay a tax we think is avoidable. We work in the open with a lot of partner teams, because the interesting problems live between systems rather than inside ours. We'd rather encode expertise into a mechanism than depend on any one person holding it, and we care more about getting the decision right than owning it.

jobs.title: Sr. Technical Program Manager - Storage, AWS Hardware Engineering, Hardware Engineering Services
jobs.description:
Application deadline: Sep 29, 2026

AWS operates the world’s largest fleet of storage servers powering exabyte-scale cloud storage services. Our team designs, builds, and operates this fleet — solving systemic hardware issues and building systems that detect and prevent recurrence so customers experience the highest quality of service.
We are seeking a Senior Technical Program Manager to drive end-to-end delivery of storage servers across our global fleet. You will coordinate cross-functional engineering teams spanning hardware, firmware, and software, manage ODM partnerships across multiple continents, and establish closed-loop quality systems that drive continuous improvements. This role requires technical depth to translate engineering constraints into program risk, combined with program management excellence to deliver complex hardware at global scale.

Key job responsibilities
RFP & ODM Selection:
Translate technical requirements into ODM evaluation criteria. Build scoring frameworks covering technical capability, manufacturing capacity, DFx maturity, automation capability, and commercial terms. Coordinate technical deep-dives between engineering and ODM design teams during competitive evaluation. Compile selection decision packages and drive decision meetings. Transition to NPI with requirements locked and statement of work signed.

NPI Program Delivery:
Facilitate requirements gathering with internal customers; develop Technical Requirements Documents (TRDs) covering server specs, rack configurations, PCIe topology, NVMe/SSD layout, power/cooling topology, and drive interconnects. Build program timelines with critical path analysis, risk identification, and milestone tracking. Own milestone-driven gate progression: manufacturing readiness, production readiness, operational readiness review, and general availability. Drive cross-functional dependencies across firmware, thermal, mechanical, and silicon teams. Communicate program status to leadership with clear reporting on milestone progress, risk posture, and mitigation plans.
Production Yield & Manufacturing Delivery
Own manufacturing readiness gates and production yield tracking from first build through volume ramp. Monitor first-pass yield by test stage, drive root cause analysis on excursions, and ensure corrective actions close before yield issues compound. Track ODM delivery cadence, line throughput, and supply chain continuity.

Fleet Operations & Feed-Forward:
Maintain fleet-level program visibility: AFR targets, unsellable resolution velocity, and component lifecycle risk. Own the feed-forward cadence — ensuring fleet failure patterns, manufacturing yield data, and vetting escapes translate into requirements and test content for next-generation programs.
Dashboards & Mechanisms
Build and own mechanisms for program visibility — defining metrics, dashboards, and review cadences that enable data-driven decisions and early risk detection. Define leading indicators: unsellable inflow/outflow rate, NPI milestone velocity, first-pass yield by test stage, and component lifecycle risk. Streamline delivery processes across teams; identify and eliminate dependencies, redundant gates, or coordination overhead that slow velocity.

Risk & Quality:
Challenge technical workstreams to surface risks early; quantify impact to schedule and reliability (annualized failure rate targets, availability SLAs) with proposed mitigations. Drive root cause analysis of fleet-wide hardware failures and ensure corrective actions flow back into qualification criteria and design requirements. Define acceptance criteria, coordinate qualification testing at server and rack levels, and manage go/no-go decisions for mission-critical storage services.
May require occasional (<10%) regional and international travel to Design and Manufacturing Partner sites.

A day in the life
You start the day syncing with ODM partners across time zones on build status and open engineering actions. Mid-morning, you run an engineering review connecting firmware, software, and hardware teams to unblock a qualification gate. In the afternoon, you lead the weekly feed-forward review — translating fleet failure patterns into test content requirements for the next-generation program. You end the day reviewing NPI milestone readiness and updating the production yield dashboard before the ODM delivery cadence call.

About the team
The Storage Server Hardware Engineering team designs and delivers the storage platforms that power Amazon S3, EBS, and other critical AWS storage services. We own our platforms cradle-to-grave: from architecture definition through NPI, manufacturing, fleet deployment, and end-of-life. Our sustaining engineers are the backbone of fleet reliability — ensuring that deployed platforms continue to meet quality and performance targets throughout their operational life.
Basic qualifications:

jobs.description:
Amazon are seeking a Technical Infrastructure Program Manager (TIPM) to support our European Data Center infrastructure growth initiatives. Based in our Dublin /London / Paris corporate & Data Center offices, the TIPM will lead cross functional teams to drive the implementation and deployment of data center expansion projects to meet the demands of our rapidly growing business.
Our Technical Program Managers are strong communicators both written and verbally and lead multi-discipline, highly technical physical infrastructure project teams. They lead teams of internal and external stakeholders through all stages of the Data Center development lifecycle from initial site due diligence, permitting through Construction and into Operation. The core role of the TIPM is to deliver capacity for our customers through developing delivery programs and working closely with stakeholder teams to identify risks and resolve issues to ensure those programs are delivered on time and within budget.

The TIPM partners with various stakeholder teams during data center delivery; Real Estate to support the feasibility and selection of new sites; Energy to ensure suitable grid connection is available; Design Engineering to coordinate project specific inputs, constraints and risks into designs; Procurement to secure on time delivery of critical equipment; Construction Management to track budget & progress; and Operations to complete the project with successful handover, to name but a few.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Key job responsibilities
Key job responsibilities
• Take large, complex projects and break them down into manageable pieces,
• Clearly communicate goals, roles, responsibilities, and desired outcomes to internal cross-functional and remote teams.
• Up to 25% travel is envisaged within EMEA.

• Work with Capacity Planning, Energy and Real Estate teams to develop short & long term build strategies to meet forecast demand.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager , Marketplace Integrations (LatAm)
jobs.description:
At Amazon LatAm we value Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) in all our job positions, therefore, we act intentionally so that our internal environment reflects the plurality of the businesses we play and the customers we serve.

About the Role
We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to own and drive the technical integration roadmap with Marketplace Hubs (Integrators) in LatAm. You will work directly with external development teams to implement, maintain, and scale their integrations to Amazon's Selling Partner API (SP-API) ecosystem, a RESTful Web service architecture that enables programmatic exchange of listings, orders, payments, reports, and more.

This role requires deep understanding of distributed systems architecture, API design patterns, and software development lifecycle, combined with strong cross-functional communication skills to engage engineering teams, negotiate timelines, and drive delivery across multiple stakeholders.

Technical Scope
Systems Architecture: Understand and advise on integration architecture patterns including event-driven architectures, webhook-based notifications, batch processing pipelines, and real-time API consumption models. Evaluate partner system designs for scalability, reliability, and compliance with Amazon's technical standards.

API and Schema Expertise: Master Amazon's SP-API framework including RESTful endpoints, JSON schema validation, OAuth 2.0 authentication flows, rate limiting strategies, error handling patterns, and data model schemas (product types, listing attributes, order objects). Guide partners through schema mapping between their internal data models and Amazon's catalog structure.

Software Development: Provide hands-on technical support including code review of integration implementations, troubleshooting HTTP request/response cycles, debugging serialization/deserialization issues, and validating payload structures. Familiarity with programming languages commonly used in integrations (Python, Java, C#, PHP, JavaScript/Node.js) is required.

AI and Automation (MCP): Leverage and advise on AI-driven automation tools, including Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations, LLM-based solutions for seller experience optimization, and intelligent automation workflows that enhance integration quality and reduce manual intervention in the development lifecycle.

Communication and Stakeholder Management: Act as the technical bridge between Amazon's internal product/engineering teams and external partner development squads. Translate complex technical requirements into actionable implementation plans. Lead technical design reviews, conduct architecture assessments, and present integration roadmaps to senior leadership.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the end-to-end integration lifecycle for a portfolio of managed integrators, from technical onboarding through production deployment and ongoing optimization
- Provide 1st and 2nd level technical consulting: documentation guidance, API best practices, example implementations, sandbox testing support, and production troubleshooting
- Analyze integration metrics (API call patterns, error rates, latency, adoption coverage) to identify improvement opportunities and drive data-informed decisions
- Manage project pipelines with daily/weekly cadence via structured communication channels, ensuring alignment on milestones, blockers, and delivery commitments
- Serve as technical advisor to Product Managers on solution feasibility, effort estimation, and product roadmap prioritization based on architectural constraints and partner capabilities
- Drive adoption of new API features and schema updates across the integrator ecosystem, ensuring rollout coverage and seller experience quality

Required Qualifications
- Experience with RESTful API architectures, Web services, and distributed systems design
- Proficiency in at least one programming language (Python, Java, C#, PHP, or JavaScript)
- Understanding of data schemas (JSON Schema, XML), API authentication (OAuth 2.0), and integration patterns (webhooks, polling, event-driven)
- Strong project management skills with ability to manage multiple concurrent technical workstreams
- Excellent verbal and written communication in Portuguese and English for cross-functional and cross-regional collaboration
- Analytical mindset with experience using metrics to drive technical decisions
- Familiarity with AI/ML concepts, automation frameworks, and emerging integration protocols (MCP)
Basic qualifications:
- 3+ years of technical product or program management experience
- 2+ years of software development experience
- 3+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
Preferred qualifications:

jobs.title: Sr. Technical Program Manager, Prime Video Sports & Live TV
jobs.description:
Every time a customer opens Prime Video during Thursday Night Football or an NBA game, dozens of systems have to publish the right broadcast, the right metadata, and the right test coverage behind the scenes before that stream ever reaches a screen. The Referee team builds the tooling that catches problems before customers do. Last year alone, our systems ran 350 million metadata verifications and tracked 34 million live event publishes end to end — work that would otherwise fall to a much larger team of manual operators.

Want to help make sure Prime Video Sports launches flawlessly every time a customer tunes in to the NFL, NBA, and more? Passionate about building the tools and processes that enable engineering teams to test complex partner integrations with confidence before they ever reach a customer? Looking forward to working in a fast-moving team of highly competent software engineers on the platforms that underpin quality for all of Prime Video Sports? Are you looking for an inclusive team, where you feel safe to be yourself, to share your ideas openly, to experiment, fail and learn, and where you help influence decisions that shape the team's path forward? If so, here is an opportunity tailored for you.

We are looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager for our team in Seattle, WA. You'll help build the testing and validation applications and services that Prime Video Sports development teams and partners rely on to verify features, partner integrations, and live event configurations before they reach customers. This is a cross-functional, high-leverage opportunity: get it right, and every sports launch across the org ships with confidence; your work will prevent issues from surfacing live, in front of customers. In this role you will work across a distributed engineering team building everything from emulator-based end-to-end testing capabilities to event configuration and timing validation tools that partner and internal teams depend on daily. If you’re a technical program manager, there’s a home for you in Seattle working on Prime Video Sports & Live TV. Our leaders are great teachers, our engineers are world-class, and our products are fun.

Key job responsibilities
You'll own program execution across our four applications, partnering with the SDM on prioritization and engineers on delivery. You will:

- Own customer intake end to end — consolidating and prioritizing requests from Prime Video Sports teams (including PAVE and Reign) and partner integrators so effort goes to the highest-impact work
- Be the interface between customer teams and engineers — shaping requirements into clear user stories, decomposing them into technical execution plans, and tracking progress against them
- Guard the customer experience of our own tools, raising the bar on usability and simplicity, and help the team make the right feature trade-offs without compromising test coverage or business relevance
- Run the mechanisms that keep the team and stakeholders aligned: intake prioritization, work tracking, and a leadership communication
- Manage cross-team dependencies and flag roadmap risk
- Balance progress on roadmap with incoming customer requests
- Build relationships across Prime Video Sports, evangelize our tools, and represent the team's tradeoffs to leadership, including in Critical Program Reviews
- Help the team adopt AI-assisted workflows in its own tooling and processes

A day in the life
Some days you're deep in a technical discussion about why TEVS test events are contending with production traffic, and whether a throttling fix or a scaling change is the right call. Other days you're writing the monthly newsletter update for leadership, or working through a backlog of customer requests to figure out what's actually worth building next quarter. The throughline is translation: turning ambiguous asks into scoped plans, and turning engineering progress into something leadership can act on.

As a Senior TPM, you will lead programs that sit across domains including Content Understanding, Content Derivatives, Artwork, Metadata, Trust and Safety. You will partner with engineering, product, science, and business leaders across Prime Video to drive technical decisions, simplify complex problem spaces, and deliver solutions that leverage ML/AI capabilities to advance our mission of being the first-stop entertainment destination for hundreds of millions of customers worldwide.

Key job responsibilities
- Lead and deliver complex programs with cross-organizational impact, operating across multiple organizations within Prime Video
- Drive clarity in ambiguous spaces where the problem, strategy, and solution path may not yet be fully defined
- Define program scope, requirements, and long-term plans for initiatives with high leadership visibility
- Identify gaps and risks across systems and teams; design simplified solutions that address constraints and deliver the best outcome
- Drive technical decisions and architectural trade-offs across engineering teams, representing benefits and challenges of each approach

- Influence stakeholders and partner teams through data-driven judgment to align on the right goals and priorities
- Build consensus across organizations, presenting complex decisions and trade-offs clearly to senior leadership

A day in the life
Your primary focus is driving complex, cross-team programs from ambiguity to delivery. On any given day, you might be defining requirements with engineering leads, clearing roadblocks across partner teams, or presenting program trade-offs to senior leadership. You will work closely with science and product teams to integrate ML/AI capabilities into customer-facing experiences. You will balance tactical execution with strategic thinking, making trade-offs between short and long-term needs. jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager, Electrical Products and Services, Data Center Engineering
jobs.description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

The Sr. Technical Program Manager drives the at-scale global implementation of the newest generations of data center electrical products and electrical distribution infrastructure technologies from concept through deployment. Just as critically, the Sr. TPM is the drum beat for product engineering and design and for New Product Introduction (NPI) into at-scale manufacturing facilities — synchronizing engineering, design, qualification, and manufacturing readiness so products transition smoothly from development into high-volume global production. This role provides a unique opportunity to engage with advanced infrastructure solutions and the exceptional people that develop them. Electrical Products and Services (EPS) within AWS Data Center Engineering designs, qualifies, manufactures, and deploys the standardized electrical products that distribute power throughout our data centers at hyperscale. Our team owns the low-voltage power distribution path from the electrical room to the rack. We productize this infrastructure to standardize and optimize power distribution package, automation, and footprint, qualify it with our suppliers, introduce it into at-scale manufacturing, , and deploy and sustain it across the global fleet (AMER, EMEA, and APAC), driving continuous generational improvements in cost, capacity, and reliability along the way.

Amazon's vision is to be the world's most customer-centric company, and this role is key to that vision. These technologies are essential for meeting our customers' expectations for service and value and meeting Amazon's goals for efficiency, speed, and reliability as we continue expanding our data centers at hyper-scale speed. We are a smart team of doers who work passionately to apply advances in data center technology. You should be comfortable driving execution in a fast-paced and often uncertain environment, and delivering results, while demonstrating leadership, technical competence, and a bias for action.

As an ideal candidate, you:

· Are passionate about understanding customers' and stakeholders' needs
· Have passion for program delivery, infrastructure execution, and low voltage products
· Are great at solving problems and removing blockers
· Have the ability to manage multiple programs/projects at different stages while staying organized
· Earn trust and build relationships with different stakeholders (e.g., Engineering, Product Development, Finance, Operations)
· Are comfortable addressing and resolving ambiguity
· Recognize and appreciate diversity of thought and perspectives

Each day you will interact with different teams responsible for engineering, product development, finance, integration, and operation of these complex technology programs. You prioritize your activities to keep programs on track, identify and resolve problems and blockers, and focus on the actions that are most impactful for delivery success.

This role requires travel of 20%+ to manufacturing facilities, AWS engineering hubs, data center sites, and supplier locations to drive NPI, qualification, and at-scale deployment.

We have an immediate opening for a Sr. Technical Program Manager in Northern Virginia, Austin, and Columbus. Seattle is a fourth and less-preferred option. If you meet these qualifications, exude passion, and enjoy the challenge of innovative projects at hyper-scale size, this job is for you!

Key job responsibilities
· Lead the cross-functional programs that design, develop, launch, and support LV power distribution, monitoring, and switching products (e.g. UL891) with $1B+ USD annual production, owning the end-to-end schedule, scope, and execution.
· Set the cadence for product engineering and design teams, driving NPI milestones and introduction into at-scale manufacturing facilities, and ensuring manufacturing readiness, qualification, and ramp targets are met.
· Engage with internal and external teams and partners to align program requirements, dependencies, and delivery commitments against rack and DC design roadmaps.
· Build detailed program plans, defining milestones, deliverables, and success criteria across engineering, qualification, and deployment workstreams.
· Coordinate between multiple teams to manage interdependencies, sequence critical path work, and secure the budget and resources required to execute product roadmaps on time.
· Identify, communicate, and mitigate program risks and blockers, and report technical status, trade-offs, and escalations to Sr. Management.
· Own and drive the complete delivery lifecycle from program kickoff through implementation, wide-scale deployment, and eventual deprecation, ensuring quality and operational readiness at each phase.
· Work independently in a high-pressure environment with all levels of leadership and exercise sound judgment where clear guidelines may not exist.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager, Alexa Shopping-Core
jobs.description:
Alexa+ is transforming how hundreds of millions of customers shop by voice, and delivering on that promise depends as much on how we build as on what we build. We're looking for a Principal Technical Program Manager to define and deliver the horizontal initiatives that raise the bar across all of Alexa Shopping — leading with the Amazon Stores Agent, the experience that lets customers complete multi-step store tasks through natural conversation on Alexa+ enabled Echo Family Devices, and extending to the cross-cutting programs, including testing and quality automation, that determine how quickly and reliably we ship. You will own a portfolio of very large, cross-organizational programs, remediate endemic problems that no single team can solve alone, and create the mechanisms that keep these programs succeeding with and without your involvement. You will work at the intersection of agentic AI research and production-quality delivery, often in areas where neither the business nor the architectural strategy has been defined, driving clarity where the problem itself is not yet clear. This is a highly visible role: you operate with complete independence, act as a force multiplier across peer teams inside and outside Alexa Shopping, and represent complex decisions and trade-offs to leaders up to three levels above (Directors and VPs). You will operate as an extension of the organization's leadership, anticipating where the org needs to go and building the programs to get it there.

Key job responsibilities
Amazon Stores Agent
-Own and scale the Amazon Stores Agent on Alexa+ enabled Echo Family Devices — launching agentic store actions that let customers complete multi-step tasks across Registries, Payments, Subscribe & Save, Addresses, Orders, and Returns by gathering what's needed through natural conversation and completing the steps on their behalf.
-Drive the program from its first actions to a customer-complete experience, holding a high task-completion bar and standing up the shared foundations — routing, evaluation, and API integration — so customers finish whole tasks hands-free and new actions ship faster over time.

Horizontal Program Leadership
-Define and own a portfolio of very large programs that cut across Alexa Shopping teams and organizations, beginning with the Amazon Stores Agent, decomposing ambiguous, org-level goals into clear workstreams that teams can execute independently.
-Anticipate future needs and stand up new horizontal initiatives before they become blockers, defining the problem, scope, success criteria, and ownership where none exist.
-Remediate critical, endemic problems that recur across teams, driving alignment among engineering, science, and product leaders on shared priorities, sequencing, and trade-offs.

Mechanisms, Metrics & Standards
-Create, optimize, and drive adoption of the metrics, reviews, and operating mechanisms that make horizontal programs measurable and durable, designed to keep succeeding with and without your involvement.
-Establish standards and best practices — including quality automation and shift-left practices that run alongside every developer, generating and executing the right tests across devices, endpoints, and geographies before a change ships — that teams across the org adopt and emulate.
-Track and communicate program health, delivery milestones, technical risks, and resource constraints to senior leadership; be the person escalations are brought to, and show excellent judgment in driving executive-level escalations.

Cross-Organizational Influence
-Build durable partnerships with peer teams across VP organizations and business lines to land programs that require coordination beyond any single org, acting as a force multiplier rather than a single-threaded doer.
-Identify risks and opportunities in technical strategies, architectures, and engineering organization structures, and influence system owners, investment, and technology direction for agentic AI systems.
-Represent complex decisions, difficult trade-offs, and potential solutions clearly, both verbally and in writing, to leaders up to three levels above, helping them understand the decisions they need to make and the options they have.

Community & Talent
-Amplify your impact by educating the TPM and engineering communities on program-management best practices, and by sharing knowledge at internal conferences and community events.
-Mentor TPMs across the organization, help managers guide their teams' career growth, and contribute to Principal TPM promotion assessments and talent reviews.
-Actively recruit for Amazon and raise the bar in the hiring and interview process.

About the team
The Alexa Shopping team owns the Shopping experiences customers use on all Alexa devices (Echo, Echo Show, Alexa App, Fire TV). With Gen AI and LLMs, we are reinventing shopping into a voice + touch experience that spans the full lifecycle - discovery, search, purchase, reorder, order tracking, and post-purchase support - across all product categories and worldwide marketplaces.

- 10+ years of engineering experience
- 7+ years of technical product or program management experience
- 5+ years of software development experience
- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
- Experience in architectural design or system design independent of an architect
- Experience in verbal and written communication for executive level leaders
- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, a related field, or equivalent experience

- Strong technical background with the judgment to evaluate end-to-end system designs (scalability, latency, reliability, quality) and to identify risks in technical strategies, architectures, and engineering organization structures.

- Experience leading testing, quality, or developer-productivity programs at scale across multiple teams.
- Experience with AI/ML products, conversational interfaces, or voice-first experiences, and a technical understanding of agentic architectures and multi-step task orchestration.
- Experience building or driving adoption of test automation and evaluation frameworks, ideally leveraging LLMs or agentic workflows.

This is a hands-on role: you will dig into technical details, work directly with data and systems, prototype solutions, and personally drive execution rather than delegating from a distance.

This role requires someone who combines deep technical judgment in distributed systems and infrastructure with the ability to operate at SVP and CEO-level strategy, someone who can architect a campaign mechanism that moves hundreds of teams, author the executive document that secures investment for it, and roll up their sleeves to unblock execution when needed.

* Guide engineering teams on architecture, design, and prioritization decisions that balance cost efficiency, service resilience, and customer latency

jobs.title: Sr. Technical Program Manager, AI Studios
jobs.description:
Join us as a Sr. Technical Program Manager on the AI Studios team within Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios, where you'll drive the delivery of AI-powered production capabilities that are transforming how movies and TV series get made. AI Studios is building Nara, an AI-native production platform that empowers professional filmmakers to create cinematic-quality animation, live action, and VFX content at unprecedented speed and scale. We are a fast-growing team operating as a startup within Amazon, with direct ownership of studio-level goals.

In this role, you are accountable for whether Live Action and VFX production capabilities ship on time and meet the technical, science, and UX quality bar required by our creative partners. You own end-to-end delivery across Engineering, Product, Applied Science, UX, and creative production teams to meet the needs of our studio's production slate. You'll translate production requirements into technical execution plans, manage cross-functional dependencies, drive prioritization decisions, and ensure delivery against ambitious milestones. This is an opportunity for exceptional TPMs who want to operate at the intersection of AI/ML and cinematic storytelling, with high ownership, autonomy, broad cross-functional influence, and direct impact on how the entertainment industry adopts AI.

Key job responsibilities
As AI Studios’ Sr. TPM, you will own end-to-end delivery for complex, cross-functional programs spanning engineering, applied science, product, and creative production teams. You will:

- Drive program delivery for live action, VFX, and digital second unit productions. Translate creative production needs into execution plans with clear milestones, dependencies, and success criteria, making scope and sequencing trade-offs to protect critical path.
- Own release readiness for your production vertical. Ensure capabilities meet production-grade quality, stability, and workflow requirements before they reach creative partners.
- Partner with Engineering and Applied Science leads on technical trade-offs across AI/ML pipelines, media processing services, model integration, and creator-facing tooling. Evaluate technical proposals, drive architecture decisions that balance production timelines with platform durability, and assess emerging AI/ML capabilities for applicability to production workflows.
- Influence engineering investment decisions and org-level prioritization by synthesizing production learnings, platform gaps, and technology trends into actionable recommendations for leadership.
- Partner with Product to shape the roadmap based on production impact and strategic alignment, and translate priorities into executable delivery plans with clear ownership and timelines.
- Own cross-team dependency management and resource coordination across multiple concurrent productions. Negotiate priorities, unblock teams, and ensure sequencing aligns capabilities to production milestone dates.
- Communicate program status, risks, and recommendations to senior leadership across Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios. Exceptional verbal and written communication is essential: you will author program narratives, decision documents, and status mechanisms that frame trade-offs clearly for executive audiences.
- Interface with creative production stakeholders (directors, VFX supervisors, producers, production managers) to understand production needs, drive prioritization of platform investments based on production impact, and close the feedback loop as capabilities land.
- Define and track program success metrics tied to creator adoption, production throughput, and platform reliability. Report on progress through business review mechanisms.
- Contribute to AI Studios programmatic leadership: design and operate the mechanisms (e.g., intake, triage, status reporting, roadmap tracking) that scale our organization as production concurrency grows. Build repeatable frameworks that enable teams to execute independently and reduce coordination overhead.

A day in the life
Your morning starts with an engineering standup where you review sprint progress and unblock a dependency between the generation pipeline and the tooling integration team. You connect with a VFX supervisor on an active production to confirm that a capability shipping this week meets their approval workflow requirements. A production partner surfaces a blocking issue hours before a creative review. You assess severity, coordinate an immediate workaround, communicate timeline to the partner, and make the call on whether to escalate or absorb.Mid-morning, you run a milestone review with Product and Science, adjusting sequencing based on a model evaluation result. After lunch, you partner on a cross-vertical mechanism (production telemetry rollout) that benefits both animation and live action. You prep a status narrative for a leadership review, then close the day by clearing a resourcing conflict between two concurrent productions vying for the same engineering capacity. Throughout, you're operating with high ownership in a fast-moving environment where AI capabilities evolve weekly and production demands are real and immediate.

About the team
AI Studios is a high-ownership team within Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios, building the AI-native production platform that is defining how cinematic content gets made with generative AI. Our team is small, fast-growing, and operates with startup intensity backed by Amazon-scale infrastructure. We work directly with professional filmmakers, animators, and VFX artists on active productions. We hold a high bar for execution, move quickly, and have direct visibility to senior leadership. If you want to work on an industry-defining product with real production stakes and ambitious creative partners, this is the role.

SAI answers a fundamental question for every item in our catalog: should Amazon carry it, surface it, and grow it? This is a strategic and complex challenges, spanning substitution science, delivery speed perception, cross-border fulfillment, and intelligent selection curation.

Within SAI, the Serra team owns two programs: Zephyr (Substitution) — which identifies nearly identical products that ship faster, arrive sooner, and cost less to fulfill — and Smart Speed, which closes the gap between operational delivery improvements and customer perception of Prime speed. Both programs operate entirely through away-team coordination, requiring alignment across SCOT, PDEX, Cart, Search, BuyX, and international marketplace teams.

The XFN (Cross-Fulfillment Network) team curates and shares domestic and cross-border selection across EU and NA stores. XFN is shifting from simply enabling all selection to intelligently deciding what selection deserves to be assorted — balancing profitability, customer demand, and cost-to-serve through AI-powered tools and selection intelligence frameworks.

jobs.description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

We’re seeking an experienced Infrastructure Technical Program Manager to oversee data center build projects in Columbus, OH. Technical Infrastructure Program Manager will lead cross-functional and technical teams from conceptual design feasibility through requirements, budget, completed design, implementation, testing, and deployment. Along the way, you will use your judgment, negotiation skills, ability to influence without authority, analytical talent, technical aptitude, and leadership to collaborate with a diverse set of stakeholders across multiple time zones, manage capital budgets, eliminate non-value-add activity, design solutions, remove blockers, and find creative ways to accelerate project delivery.

The successful candidate will be a strong communicator (both written and verbal), not be hindered by ambiguity or competing priorities, and be capable of understanding mechanical/electrical engineering concepts. They will be able to apply a variety of project management tools, methodologies and techniques for all phases of the project lifecycle and exhibit demonstrated experience in tactical project management of highly technical initiatives and core project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, resources, quality and risk management, reporting and metric development/tracking. Other requirements include experience with MS Office, MS Project and MS SharePoint. Experience with Tableau, KanBan, Playbook, SQL and systems integration is a plus.

If you enjoy the challenges of deploying highly technical and innovative projects at massive scale, this job is for you!

About the team
Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Key job responsibilities
• You’ll drive both network hardware and software programs to meet the ever-growing customer demand.
• You’ll manage competing cross-organizational projects/programs on a global scale.
• You’ll interact cross-team Network Managers, cross-team Technical Program Managers, Engineers, and Data Center Technicians and senior management.

• You’ll work with engineers to develop detailed and creative solutions to complex problems, while keeping a watchful-eye on timelines and costs.
• You’ll drive simplification efforts in engineering and project/program management, and architectures to unblock innovation.

A day in the life
Technical Program Managers in the BERE organization have a wide range of responsibilities: we work with internal partners to develop and implement the next gen infrastructures along with the tooling ecosystems to support with these platforms driving efficiency and scalability through the automation of builds, configuration deployment, and the scaling of capacity. If that question excites you, keep reading. We're looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to lead the strategy and execution of programs across Last Mile Delivery. At Amazon, we're working to be the most Customer-centric company on earth. One customer experience that we’re constantly looking to take to a new level is how we fulfill and deliver their orders. Our Last Mile organization is at the forefront of this mission: pioneering new products and services, partnering with Delivery Service Partners and Amazon Flex, and building a world-class operation that spans North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific. As part of Amazon Delivery's PRISM (Central TPM) organization, you will own the end-to-end program strategy for last mile initiatives, driving cross-functional alignment across business, product, and engineering teams to launch and scale programs that move the needle on delivery. You will partner with senior leaders across multiple organizations to define priorities, remove blockers, and deliver results.

The ideal candidate thrives in ambiguity, brings strong business and technical judgment, and has a track record of delivering complex programs. You are a crisp communicator who can influence at the VP level and translate business goals into actionable roadmaps. If you want to solve one of the most challenging problems in logistics, making delivery faster for every customer, everywhere, this is your role.

Key job responsibilities
- Serve as the single-threaded leader owning complex programs across multiple VP organizations
- Identify business and technical requirements with science, operations, product, and engineering stakeholders, translating them into specifications, scoped deliverables, and program roadmap from design through launch
- Lead design and implementation efforts across cross-functional teams, making trade-offs to optimize time-to-market
- Own stakeholder communication through all stages of the product lifecycle, clearly articulating goals, roles, and desired outcomes
- Drive high-level strategic initiatives while being willing to roll up your sleeves and get the job done

The right candidate will have a strong program management background, demonstrated experience leading large to extra-large projects, and a well-rounded technical foundation. You must thrive in an entrepreneurial environment and not be hindered by ambiguity or competing priorities.

You will run strategic reviews, unblock cross-functional dependencies, and make trade-off decisions that keep programs on track.
